items.title: PhD Researcher: AI-driven Employee-Customer Relationship Management in the Service Sector
items.desc: Please note that Dutch at the B2 level is required for this vacancy. Do you have a passion for business-relevant research and the ambition to obtain your PhD on the hot topic of creating business value with data analytics and AI? Do you have the right academic background and are you ready to start this 4-year journey in our open, international and collegial environment? Let’s meet! PhD Researcher: AI-driven Employee-Customer Relationship Management in the Service Sector Vlerick Business School is an innovative, top-ranked and sustainable international business school in the heart of Europe. Our purpose is to transform people for a better world! We want being at Vlerick to be a transformative experience where you discover the knowledge, mindset and confidence you need to take your next leap – and become the entrepreneurial leader our world needs. Glowi is a dynamic group offering innovative services across multiple domains to make life easier for individuals and businesses. Its business units include Het Poetsbureau & Easy Life (Glowi Home); Friends of Cartel (Marketing Solutions), Glowi Jobs and Motmans & Partners (HR Solutions). Together, they combine expertise and passion to create solutions that truly make a difference. As a Belgian company, Glowi is at the forefront of innovation in the cleaning services sector, combining operational excellence with data-driven insights to transform how clients and cleaners connect. With a strong focus on decentralised communication, performance tracking, and human-centric consultancy, Glowi empowers its teams to deliver measurable impact across cleaner acquisition, client retention, and administrative efficiency. The company’s commitment to continuous improvement and smart technology integration makes it a catalyst for change in a traditionally manual industry. Their main office in Beringen . At Glowi, data is an important asset that can be transformed into business value through innovative AI-based methodologies. In a collaboration with Vlerick Business School, Glowi wants to research these opportunities. We are looking for a business-oriented data scientist to develop and research AI opportunities in the service sector with academic rigour. As part of our close-knit team, you’ll bring Vlerick’s strategy and purpose to life. Are you excited to join our Area Marketing & Sales team as a PhD Researcher? Here’s what you need to know! Your Mission You will combine academic research with direct business impact, translating data and AI insights into real-world applications. Academic focus Complete a 4-year PhD on data analytics and AI. Conduct academic and applied research, including data collection, modelling, AI agent development, evaluation and reporting. Disseminate insights through papers, reports, workshops, presentations and social media for both academic and business audiences. Collaborate with faculty, researchers and support the activities of the research area. Business impact Work with client and employee data from Glowi. Develop predictive models and AI-driven solutions that are operationalised within the organisation. Design and evaluate genAI-supported workflows and AI agents embedded in existing processes. Work closely with Glowi’s Data & AI team and business stakeholders to improve key business KPIs. The Research Your PhD research will focus on employee-customer relationship management (acquisition, development and retention) within the cleaning services sector , exploring how machine learning and AI agents can generate insights and improve processes. The exact research topic will be defined together with the PhD candidate and may include: AI-driven employee and customer acquisition Consultant coaching effects on development and churn Skills, knowledge and behaviour (KSB) matching in recruitment and retention Employee absenteeism and performance modelling Pricing and price sensitivity analysis Hyper-personalised employee and customer communication using genAI Process automation using genAI and reinforcement learning All research is conducted in close collaboration with the business and combines state-of-the-art technology, real-world data, advanced modelling, and academic and managerial reporting. You Obtained a master’s degree in business analytics, business engineering, artificial intelligence, data science, business administration, economics, computer science, civil engineering, statistics, mathematics, or equivalent. Have excellent qualifications during your studies, such as distinctions (cum laude or higher) at the bachelor's and master's levels. Have good communication skills and a business mindset, which allows you to easily switch between different stakeholders at all levels. Can take up responsibilities and work independently. Are passionate about the topic, have a research mindset and great analytical skills. Have a good knowledge of data analytics and machine learning. Can program and have experience with Python and SQL. Preferably have experience with Microsoft Fabric and Azure. Are fluent in Dutch and English and have excellent writing skills. Have a proactive attitude and don’t shy away from presenting your findings to an academic and business audience. Will be based on one of our Vlerick campuses (Ghent or Brussels) and the office of Glowi at #ProudtobeVlerick Autonomy and responsibility in an engaging work environment. A dynamic, open, and international company culture. Opportunities for professional and personal growth. A team of enthusiastic, driven colleagues, passionate about learning. Opportunities to build your network, both in academics and in business. You’ll have a real impact and inspire people to live, learn and leap! At Vlerick, openness to the world is part of our DNA. We are continuously working towards being a truly diverse, equitable and inclusive place to work and learn at. So, no matter who you are, where you come from, or what your dreams are, we are looking forward to receiving your application. Vlerick Business School is the hosting institute for this PhD journey with Philippe Baecke as your promoter. Your salary will be in line with the salary scales at Ghent University. More information on the salary can be transparently accessed via this link. Take the leap! In case you are interested in this PhD journey and meet the mentioned criteria, please apply with your resume, motivation letter and transcripts from both your bachelor’s and master’s degree via our website. If available, please also add the results of your TOEFL or IELTS and your GRE score . We look forward to hearing from you! Happy to give you more information on the job content: philippe.baecke@vlerick.com. For more information on the selection process, please reach out to charlotte.mahieu@vlerick.com.

items.title: PhD position – Electromagnetic Compatibility & AI (all genders)
items.desc: Silicon Austria Labs (SAL), in collaboration with the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), is seeking a motivated PhD candidate to work on the AI-assisted modelling and prediction of radiated electromagnetic emissions from power electronics converters. The PhD project will be co-supervised by SAL and SDU. The candidate will spend most of the project period at SAL in Austria, working closely with SAL researchers to develop power electronics use cases for industry. The candidate will also receive academic supervision and scientific guidance from SDU, nevertheless the workplace is Graz. The PhD project combines the fields of power electronics, electromagnetic compatibility, radiated emission measurements, electromagnetic simulation, and AI-based modelling. The project aims to develop practical methods to help identify dominant radiation mechanisms, predict emission levels, and support EMC-aware converter design. Your Future Tasks Include Research topic Possible Research Directions Include Physics-informed AI models for predicting radiated emissions. Data-driven surrogate models for fast electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) assessment of converter designs. Modelling of dominant radiation sources, current loops, switching nodes, cables, heat sinks and PCB structures. Use of simulation and measurement data for AI model training and validation. Development of practical workflows for the early-stage design of EMC-aware power electronics. The project will not primarily focus on conducted emissions, but may consider source and coupling mechanisms where they influence the behaviour of radiated emissions. Main Tasks Develop AI/ML and physics-informed modelling methods for predicting radiated emissions. Work with power electronic converter models, electromagnetic simulations and measurement data. Analyse dominant radiation mechanisms in converter systems. Build and validate surrogate models for fast radiated emission estimation. Compare AI-assisted methods with conventional EMC simulation and measurement approaches. Develop benchmark and validation cases based on realistic converter structures. Publish results. Your Profile A Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Electromagnetics, Applied Physics or Computer Science. Very good understanding of power electronics, EMI/EMC, electromagnetic fields and circuit/system modelling. Programming experience, preferably in Python, MATLAB or similar tools. Interest in machine learning, surrogate modelling, scientific machine learning, or physics-informed AI. Ability to work independently and in an interdisciplinary research environment Experience with one or more of the following is advantageous: Radiated emission measurements or EMC testing Power converter modelling and high-frequency switching behaviour Electromagnetic simulation tools Near-field scanning Machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow Physics-informed neural networks or hybrid physics-AI modelling Signal processing and data analysis Important Facts About SAL Diverse research activities with many technical challenges. State-of-the-art laboratory facilities and equipment. Location in the heart of Europe in Austria – relocation support for non-European nationalities. Internal and external training opportunities for career development. Family & children friendly - actively shaping the compatibility of family and career. “Vital4SAL” to promote a healthy workplace (e.g. SAL coaching pool, trainings on mental health, physical activities, healthy snacks, 24/7 accident insurance) € 4 per day meal allowance in restaurants or € 2 per working day in supermarkets. Public transport initiative (subsidy for the “Klimaticket”) Our values: Open door policy, flexibility in working hours, casual dress code, diverse teams, working with people of different nationalities, informal communication, lifelong learning, compatibility of family and career, sustainability, personal growth, and collective advancement. This position is advertised in accordance with the collective agreement for employees in non-university research (Research CA). For this position, we offer a 3 years limited contract with the focus on pursuing the PhD. For this position, your monthly salary will be EUR 3.651, paid 14 times a year (based on an All-in contract). About Us Silicon Austria Labs (SAL) is a top research center for Electronics and Software Based Systems (ESBS). At three locations (Graz, Villach, Linz), SAL is conducting research along the entire ESBS value chain in the areas of sensor systems, power electronics, intelligent wireless systems, microsystems and embedded systems to develop future-oriented solutions for industrial production, health, energy, mobility, safety and more. SAL brings together key players from industry, science and research and thus valuable expertise and know-how and conducts cooperative, application-oriented research along the value chain. Cooperative projects are co-financed by SAL and enable a fast and unbureaucratic project start. SAL is thus shaping the high-tech location Austria and Europe and developing the future. Innovation is our top priority and so are our employees. We are a family-friendly company and support the compatibility of work and family as much as possible. That is why we have been awarded the Work and Family Certificate until 2026. But we are constantly working on new measures to offer our employees an environment where they feel good, healthy and motivated.

items.title: PhD Candidate in Explainable Machine Learning for Studying Biology at Single-Cell Resolution
items.desc: Are you a MSc graduate with background in data science, computer science, biostatistics, bioinformatics or a related field? Do you have a solid foundation in machine learning? Are you passionate about biology and interested in building new machine learning and AI to accelerate biological discoveries? Then this position is for you! Working at the UvA Join Us! We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop novel methodology for the analysis of single-cell (multi)-omics data by incorporating existing biological knowledge into machine learning models. You will join a collaborative and internationally-oriented team working at the interface of computer science, mathematics, and biology in the Biosystems Data Analysis group at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences at the University of Amsterdam. We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. If you recognise yourself in the role but do not meet every listed preference, we encourage you to apply. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do Interpretable machine learning is a growing research area, with important applications in the biological sciences, such as understanding how different genes regulate each other within biological pathways. However, the current common practice is first to build complicated, “black-box” models and try to understand what they learned afterwards. This has the disadvantage that a) interpretation is still not always possible and b) it is inefficient as the model must re-discover patterns that are already well-known from scratch every time it is trained. Recent technological advances have allowed us to study DNA and RNA not only in a “bulk” tissue, but also at a single-cell resolution, giving us unprecedented insights into how organisms form, how diseases develop, and how cells communicate with each other inside a tissue. In this project, you will build interpretable-by-design machine learning models for biological data that offer biological insights in a direct way. Such models will be applicable to a variety of single-cell datasets and experiments in different fields of biology. Tasks and responsibilities: complete a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration (four years); develop novel algorithms for analyzing single-cell (multi)-omics data and design and perform in silico experiments to test them; be an active and responsible member of the research group and collaborate closely with fellow group members; discuss work with group members and at departmental meetings, and incorporate feedback; take a leading role in writing manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and conferences; participate in the PhD training programme of the University of Amsterdam; assist with teaching and supervision of Bachelor’s and Master’s students. You will have the opportunity to: work at the interface of machine learning and biology; collaborate closely with biologists from a variety of disciplines including immunology and cancer biology; present results at national and international scientific conferences; expand academic, professional and personal skills; use high-end compute infrastructure via the national ICT cooperative (SURF) What We Ask Of You You are passionate about research and want to develop into an independent scientist. You have a background in machine learning and artificial intelligence and like to build novel methods for the analysis of biological data. You are methodical, curious and able to take initiative, while also valuing close collaboration in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. Your Experience And Profile You hold a MSc in Bioinformatics, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Biostatistics or a closely related discipline; have demonstrable experience with training machine and deep learning models, preferably using Python; have a basic understanding of biology and/or are interested in using computational methods to understand biology; are fluent in English, written and spoken. Your place at the UvA About The Faculty Of Science Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, whether it concerns elementary particles, the birth of the universe, or how the brain functions. The Faculty has a student population of approximately 8,000 students, as well as 1,800 staff members working in education, research, or support services. Important to know Your application & contact If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the apply button. We accept applications until and including 31 October 2026. Do you have any questions, or do you require additional information? Please contact: dr. ir. Stavros Makrodimitris, s.makrodimitris@uva.nl prof. Dr. Aalt-Jan van Dijk, a.d.j.vandijk@uva.nl. Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file): a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience; a letter of motivation; the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation. A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure. (for details: national knowledge security guidelines) Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion As an employer, the UvA maintains an equal opportunities policy. We value diversity and are fully committed to being a place where everyone feels at home. We nurture inquisitive minds and perseverance and allow room for persistent questioning. With us, curiosity and creativity are the prevailing culture. Studies show that women and members of underrepresented groups only apply for jobs if they meet 100% of the qualifications. Do you meet the educational requirements but not yet all of the requested experience? The UvA encourages you to apply anyway.

items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Predictive Modelling of Reused Concrete Elements
items.desc: About Us The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character. The Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) at the University of Luxembourg contributes multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine. Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in. The Sustainable Concrete Structure Laboratory is looking for 3 new Ph.D. candidates based on the ERC project RESCUE. In this fully-funded position, the Ph.D. candidates will work on using developing new modelling frameworks for predicting the remaining life of reused concrete elements. This project calls for an open character with a strong knowledge on concrete structures as well as curiosity across discipline boundaries (civil engineering, material science, and computer science). Your role As the successful candidate, you will contribute to a research project at the intersection of engineering (concrete structures), material science (durability, mechanical behavior), data science (probabilistic modelling, ML, multi-scale, …), and life-cycle analyses. The aim of these Ph.D. projects is to develop the first predictive modelling for reused concrete-element capacity. The tasks comprise the development of a laboratory campaign of full-scale reused concrete elements, the development of non-destructive testing methods, the development of new data-driven physics-informed models, and the evaluations of life-cycle gains. This groundbreaking research output will lead to the extension of the service life of concrete infrastructures, leading to a significant reduction of carbon emissions and costs of the construction sector. PhD topics: First PhD topic: Mechanical behavior of reused concrete Second PhD topic: Durability properties of reused concrete Third PhD topic: Data-driven modelling of reused concrete We do not expect every single person to be an expert across all these fields, but you must be open to learning about and embracing challenges in fields you may not yet have been working with. We thus warmly encourage you to apply even if you feel that you only partially meet the criteria in terms of background and expertise, as you will have the opportunity to acquire the missing knowledge during the first year of the project. Your profile Master’s degree (or equivalent) in civil engineering or related area Good understanding of the structural behavior and material properties of concrete structures and modelling of civil structures. Knowledge of concrete reuse is a plus Curiosity, a genuine passion for scientific research Commitment and capacity to critical thinking and good research ethics Operational Language Requirements: Excellent command of English is required Academic Eligibility (Thesis): Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission – Doctoral Candidates. We offer A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs How to apply Applications should include: Curriculum Vitae Cover letter presenting your motivation for this project, explaining why do you want to work for a Ph.D. degree and why at the University of Luxembourg Transcript of all modules and results from university-level courses taken List of publications (if available) or work samples (5 pages max) PDF version of your Master Thesis with English abstract Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. In line with our values, the University of Luxembourg promotes an inclusive culture. Nos engagements, vos avantages Une réussite portée par notre excellence technologique, votre expérience et notre ambition partagée Un package de rémunération attractif Un développement des compétences en continu : parcours de formation, académies et communautés internes Un environnement inclusif, bienveillant et respectant l’équilibre des collaborateurs Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu Votre quotidien Thales Research&Technology, notre centre de recherche dans les domaines matériels, et CortAIx Labs, notre centre de recherche en IA et digital ont pour mission de proposer des innovations de ruptures, de maintenir et d’accroitre l’avance technologique et d’en assurer la compétitivité pour le groupe. En nous rejoignant, vous intégrerez le laboratoire d’Intelligence Artificielle et Perception Avancée de Thales Research & Technology. Les travaux de recherche menés au sein du laboratoire visent à développer de nouvelles approches d’intelligence artificielle pour les systèmes de perception, dans des environnements où les données sont rares, hétérogènes et coûteuses à acquérir, notamment pour des capteurs spécialisés tels que l’infrarouge (IR), le sonar ou les systèmes multi-spectraux. Dans Le Cadre De Cette Thèse, Vous Contribuerez Au Développement De Modèles Génératifs Multimodaux Capables De Générer des données synthétiques réalistes et automatiquement annotées à partir de jeux de données limités ; Améliorer la qualité d’images et de vidéos dégradées ; Réaliser des transferts inter-modaux entre différentes modalités de capteurs (RGB, IR, sonar, multi-spectral) ; Modéliser la dynamique temporelle des scènes afin de produire des vidéos cohérentes ; Exploiter les représentations sémantiques issues des Vision-Language Models (VLMs) pour guider et contraindre la génération. Vos travaux s’articuleront autour de deux axes principaux : Génération de données synthétiques et apprentissage frugal : étude et développement de modèles génératifs de nouvelle génération (diffusion, flow matching, rectified flows) pour la création d’images et de vidéos réalistes à partir de peu d’exemples ; Génération multimodale et transfert inter-capteurs : conception de modèles capables de générer automatiquement des modalités rares telles que l’infrarouge ou le sonar à partir de données plus abondantes comme les images RGB. Enfin, vous participerez à la conception, au développement et à l’évaluation de ces modèles, ainsi qu’à l’analyse de leur apport pour les applications de perception, de classification, de détection et de segmentation. items.desc: Wasserstoff gilt als einer der zentralen Hoffnungsträger für die Energiewende und wird eine Schlüsselrolle in der Defossilierung von Industrie, Mobilität und Energiesystemen einnehmen. Im Zuge der Elektrifizierung des Antriebsstrangs rücken zugleich die Schwingungs- und Akustikeigenschaften moderner Fahrzeuge stärker in den Fokus der Produktentwicklung: Während klassische Verbrennungsmotorgeräusche wegfallen, treten neue Geräuschquellen in den Vordergrund und auch der Leichtbau verändert das dynamische Verhalten der Fahrzeugstruktur nachhaltig. Ihre Forschung verbindet diese beiden Zukunftsfelder. In Ihrer Forschung befassen Sie sich zum einen mit der systemischen Analyse und Optimierung von Brennstoffzellen, Batterien und Elektrolyseuren auf der übergeordneten System- und Betriebsebene. Zum anderen untersuchen Sie das Schwingungs- und Akustikverhalten von Fahrzeugkomponenten unter anderem im Spannungsfeld zwischen NVH-Verhalten und Leichtbau. Ziel ist es, durch geeignete Betriebsstrategien Effizienz, Lebensdauer und Wirtschaftlichkeit der Energietechnologien im realen Einsatz zu maximieren und zugleich mittels gemisch physisch-virtueller Valdiderung das strukturdynamische und akustische Verhalten von Bauteilen und Fahrzeugen zu charakterisieren und gezielt zu optimieren. items.title: PhD in Acoustic Performance of Timber Structure Connections
items.desc: Introduction Are you fascinated by improving the acoustic performance of timber buildings? Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. Jonas Brunskog (DTU, with expertise in the acoustics of lightweight structures). You will be based in the Building Acoustics research group (https://building-acoustics.net/) in the Department of the Built Environment at TU/e, and will spend approximately six months at DTU’s Acoustic Technology group in Denmark. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in acoustics, building physics, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or related disciplines. A research-oriented attitude. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). The following experience could be considered an advantage and may be highlighted in your motivation letter: Affinity for building acoustics, vibro-acoustics, or structural dynamics Previous experience with/affinity for computational methods Previous publications and scientific communications Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. items.desc: Projet de thèse CIFRE — Apprentissage de stratégies de mémoire et de décision pour des systèmes d’IA locaux Mots-clés : Agentic systems, LLMs, persistent memory, sequential decision-making, reinforcement learning, model routing, model specialization, sovereign AI. Contexte scientifique USTS développe un projet d’IA souveraine, entièrement exécuté sur une infrastructure locale, pour permettre aux entreprises de garder le contrôle de leurs données et de leurs systèmes, tout en préservant la précision et la qualité des résultats. La thèse s’intéresse aux systèmes fondés sur des modèles de langage capables d’accomplir des tâches séquentielles : exploiter des informations, interagir avec des outils, conserver des connaissances et adapter leurs actions aux résultats obtenus. Dans ce cadre, la réussite dépend de décisions prises à différents moments de l’exécution, dont les conséquences peuvent être différées. Le choix d’une information à conserver influence les actions futures. Le choix d’un modèle détermine le coût et la qualité d’une étape. Une vérification peut éviter la propagation d’une erreur, mais consomme des ressources supplémentaires. La mémoire, les actions et l’utilisation des modèles constituent ainsi des composantes interdépendantes du processus de décision. Le problème étudié sera celui de l’apprentissage de stratégies coordonnées pour ces composantes, dans un environnement où les informations évoluent et où le calcul disponible est limité. Question scientifique et hypothèses Comment apprendre conjointement des stratégies de mémoire, d’action et d’utilisation des modèles qui maintiennent la fiabilité des tâches séquentielles lorsque les informations évoluent et que les ressources de calcul sont limitées ? Une hypothèse centrale est que l’apprentissage de ces stratégies à partir de la réussite des tâches complètes peut améliorer le compromis entre fiabilité et coût de calcul par rapport à des stratégies optimisées séparément. Cette hypothèse conduit à plusieurs questions : comment estimer l’utilité future d’une information ? Comment attribuer un échec à une décision de mémoire, à une action ou au choix d’un modèle ? Comment répartir les ressources entre génération, recherche d’information et vérification ? Dans quelles conditions les stratégies apprises restent-elles efficaces sur de nouvelles tâches ? Ces questions seront étudiées à travers des hypothèses explicites et des expériences permettant de les confirmer, de les réfuter ou d’en préciser les conditions de validité. Programme de recherche Les premiers travaux porteront sur la formalisation du système comme un problème de décision séquentielle, éventuellement partiellement observable. Il s’agira de définir les observations accessibles, les opérations de mémoire, les actions possibles et les contraintes de ressources. Cette formulation permettra d’étudier des objectifs d’apprentissage combinant réussite de la tâche, erreurs et coût d’exécution. L’apprentissage de la mémoire La recherche portera sur la sélection, la représentation, la mise à jour et la récupération des informations en fonction de leur utilité pour les décisions futures. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux informations corrigées ou devenues obsolètes, ainsi qu’aux conséquences différées des opérations de mémoire. L’attribution des erreurs et l’apprentissage des décisions Lorsque l’évaluation porte sur le résultat final, il peut être difficile d’identifier les décisions responsables d’un échec. Les travaux pourront étudier des signaux intermédiaires, des objectifs auxiliaires ou des méthodes d’attribution permettant d’améliorer l’apprentissage sans réduire l’évaluation à la qualité de chaque étape prise isolément. L’allocation adaptative du calcul Le système devra choisir quand mobiliser un modèle spécialisé, solliciter un modèle plus coûteux, rechercher une information ou vérifier un résultat. L’objectif sera d’apprendre ces choix en fonction de l’état de la tâche, de l’incertitude et des ressources restantes. Ces volets contribueront à une même problématique. Leur articulation et leur priorité seront précisées à partir de l’état de l’art et des premiers résultats expérimentaux. Recherche sur les modèles Les modèles constituent le moteur du système étudié. La thèse comprendra donc des travaux sur les modèles génératifs, les modèles de décision et leurs modalités d’apprentissage. Les recherches pourront porter sur la spécialisation de modèles locaux, la distillation de comportements ou la conception d’objectifs d’entraînement tenant compte de la réussite de trajectoires complètes. Elles examineront également la répartition des capacités entre un modèle unique et un ensemble de modèles coordonnés par une politique de routage. L’enjeu sera de déterminer quelles capacités doivent être apprises dans les modèles et quelles décisions doivent être prises au cours de l’exécution. Les architectures seront comparées en intégrant le coût de leur coordination et les interactions entre spécialisation, mémoire et décision. Évaluation et contributions attendues L’évaluation reposera sur des tâches séquentielles permettant de faire varier la durée des trajectoires, l’évolution des informations, la disponibilité des outils et les budgets de calcul. Des comparaisons avec des méthodes de référence, des études d’ablation et des évaluations sur des tâches non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage permettront d’identifier l’origine des gains et leurs limites. Les mesures porteront notamment sur la réussite des tâches, les erreurs critiques, la stabilité des résultats, la latence et les ressources consommées. Les expériences étudieront également la propagation des erreurs et la capacité du système à récupérer après une décision incorrecte. Les applications métier serviront à confronter les méthodes aux conditions d’utilisation réelles. Pour un métier et un ensemble de tâches définis, l’objectif sera d’étudier dans quelles conditions un système local peut atteindre une qualité comparable ou proche de celle de solutions généralistes accessibles au public. Cet objectif sera évalué selon des critères et une marge d’écart définis à l’avance. Les contributions attendues pourront comprendre une formulation du problème, des méthodes d’apprentissage originales et une caractérisation expérimentale de leurs propriétés, de leur capacité de généralisation et de leurs limites. Les résultats donneront lieu à des publications scientifiques et à des expérimentations reproductibles. Profil recherché Vous êtes titulaire d’un master 2 ou d’un diplôme d’ingénieur en informatique, intelligence artificielle, mathématiques appliquées ou dans un domaine proche. Vous avez de solides connaissances en machine learning et en modèles de langage, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de Python et d’un framework d’apprentissage profond tel que PyTorch. Des connaissances en apprentissage par renforcement, en décision séquentielle, en statistiques ou en optimisation seront appréciées. Vous souhaitez mener un travail de recherche et avez une appétence pour les solutions d’IA et l’ingénierie nécessaire à leur expérimentation. Vous savez formuler des hypothèses, concevoir des expériences et analyser leurs résultats. Conditions et candidature Durée : 36 mois. Lieu : La Réunion. Début : à convenir avec le laboratoire d’accueil. Rémunération : ... Moyens de calcul : serveurs équipés de plusieurs GPU. Encadrement USTS : Hugo. Laboratoire d’accueil et direction de thèse : à préciser. Financement envisagé : dispositif CIFRE. Pour candidater, envoyez votre CV et un court texte présentant votre intérêt pour le sujet à recrutement@usts.ai. Vous pouvez joindre un mémoire, un article ou un projet illustrant votre expérience. Rémunération : 26 000,00€ à 30 000,00€ par an Avantages : Prise en charge du transport quotidien Lieu du poste : En présentiel

items.title: Wissenschaftliche MitarbeiterIn – DoktorandIn (PhD)
items.desc: Die Process and Data Science Gruppe (PADS) sucht kontinuierlich nach talentierten neuen MitarbeiterInnen, die an der Schnittstelle von Data Science und Process Science arbeiten möchten. Es gibt offene Stellen auf allen Ebenen (PhD, Postdoc, Software Engineer, etc.). Bei Interesse senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung bitte direkt an applications@pads.rwth-aachen.de Wenn Sie sich bewerben, geben Sie bitte relevante Informationen an und begründen Sie, warum Sie zu unserer Forschung im Bereich Process Mining beitragen können. Generische Bewerbungen werden aussortiert. Zeigen Sie, dass Sie wissen, was die Gruppe tut und was Sie zum Stand der Technik im Process Mining beitragen wollen. Bitte beachten Sie, dass das PADS-Schwerpunktkolloquium für Personen gedacht ist, die sich auf PADS-bezogene Themen spezialisieren möchten, d.h. auf Process Mining oder andere Ansätze, die Prozess- und Datenwissenschaft miteinander verbinden. Lesen Sie unbedingt das Springer-Buch "Process Mining: Data Science in Action" (ISBN: 978-3-662-49850-7) ausführlich und seien Sie darauf vorbereitet, technische Fragen zu den von Ihnen belegten PADS-Kursen zu beantworten (z.B. konkrete Modelle anhand von Daten zu erstellen). Der beste Zeitpunkt für das mündliche PADS- Schwerpunktkolloquium ist kurz vor der Masterarbeit. Studierenden mit schlechteren Noten in den BPI/APM/IDS-Kursen wird dringend empfohlen, ein anderes Schwerpunktkolloquium zu wählen oder sich sehr gut vorzubereiten. Es ist gewünscht, dass sich StudentInnen bewerben, welche Ihre Masterarbeit in unserer Gruppe schreiben möchten. Alle Stellen sind grundsätzlich Vollzeitstellen, es besteht aber auch die Möglichkeit, in Teilzeit zu arbeiten. Die Vergütung erfolgt in Anlehnung an den Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) unter Berücksichtigung Ihrer Berufserfahrung. Die RWTH ist ein Arbeitgeber der Chancengleichheit. Wir freuen uns daher über Bewerbungen von allen qualifizierten Bewerberinnen und Bewerbern, insbesondere aus derzeit benachteiligten Personengruppen. Ihre Ansprechpartnerin Frau Mara Nitschke Tel.: +49 (0) 241 8021902 E-Mail: applications@pads.rwth-aachen.de Wissenschaftliche MitarbeiterIn – DoktorandIn (PhD) Als DoktorandIn haben Sie die Möglichkeit, in einem Bereich mit vielen offenen wissenschaftlichen Herausforderungen zu forschen. Sie werden eine begrenzte Lehraufgabe haben und Bachelor- und MasterstudentInnen betreuen. In einem Zeitraum von vier Jahren erhalten Sie ausreichend Zeit, um Spitzenforschung zu betreiben und Ihre Arbeit auf den führenden Konferenzen in diesem Bereich zu präsentieren. Sie werden in einer starken und fokussierten Forschungsgruppe arbeiten, in der Sie die erforderliche Unterstützung und Rückmeldung erhalten. Nach einem PhD in PADS können Sie wählen, ob Sie eine Karriere in der Industrie oder in der Wissenschaft anstreben wollen. Der Grund dafür ist, dass Process Mining herausfordernde Forschungsprobleme bietet und gleichzeitig ein großer Bedarf an Experten besteht, die an der Schnittstelle von Prozessen und Daten arbeiten. Anforderungen Ein Master-Abschluss in Informatik oder Data Science (oder einer benachbarten Disziplin wie Operations Research, Elektrotechnik und Statistik) Sie verfügen über ausgezeichnete Sprachkenntnisse in Englisch und sind bereit, Ihre Ideen zu präsentieren. Sie sind in der Lage, Forschungsprototypen (z. B. in Java oder Python) zu entwickeln, um groß angelegte Experimente durchzuführen. Sie legen Wert auf Präzision, d. h. Sie sind bestrebt, Ihre Ideen rigoros zu präsentieren und zu prüfen. Sie kennen sich mit Process Mining aus (lesen Sie z. B. die process mining book oder den Coursera MOOC besucht "Process Mining: Data science in Action"). Sie haben ein echtes Interesse und/oder Erfahrung in den Bereichen Data Science, Process Science, Process Mining, maschinelles Lernen, Prozessmanagement und/oder Operations Research.

items.title: PhD Researcher / Doctoral Researcher (m/f/d) Bioinformatics & AML
items.desc: Department of Internal Medicine II, Research Group: Functional Genomics of Acute Leukemia (Heads: Dr. Lorenz Bastian / Prof. Dr. Claudia Baldus) The position is part of the newly established research project “LUCID-AML – Learning-based Unsupervised Clustering of transcriptomIcs to Detect developmental, functional and prognostic subtypes in AML across age”, funded by the Deutsche José Carreras Leukämie-Stiftung. It is closely linked to our DFG-funded Clinical Research Unit “CATCH-ALL: Towards a Cure for Adults and Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia”, where clinical and basic researchers work together to define mechanisms of leukemogenesis and treatment resistance across age groups. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) affects people of all ages, but its incidence increases steeply in older adults, while survival decreases sharply with age. AML can be classified into transcriptomic groups that reflect cytogenetic lesions, reveal developmental origins and link leukemias to normal hematopoietic states. However, consistent subtype definitions and robustly validated tools for applying them across cohorts are lacking. The project builds on ALLCatchR and our work on machine-learning frameworks for disease classification and the identification of novel molecular subtypes in acute lymphoblastic leukemia. LUCID-AML will integrate more than 8,000 bulk AML gene-expression profiles from multiple cohorts with single-cell data, molecular genetics, diagnostic classifications, drug-response data and clinical outcomes. The project aims to establish reproducible, gene-expression-based AML subtypes while accounting for age and treatment. Further aims are to define their developmental origins and make the resulting models available as transparent, open-source tools for research and clinical diagnostics. For further reading: Beder et al., HemaSphere, 2023; Bastian et al., Blood, 2024; Beder et al., bioRxiv / HemaSphere, 2026. Join our team Join our team as soon as possible . The initial appointment is for three years , with the possibility of extension . What we offer: Remuneration according to the German TV-L E13 pay scale for a 65% position (25 hours per week), subject to the applicable collective agreement requirements; the position offers the opportunity to pursue a PhD Access to a large AML transcriptomics resource with comprehensive molecular, functional and clinical annotations across a broad age range Close collaboration with computational and clinical scientists, bioinformaticians, experimental hematologists and clinician-scientists, including national and international partners Training and research opportunities in large-scale bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, R package development and reproducible research, with access to high-performance computing infrastructure Additional UKSH employee benefits according to institutional policies: Benefits Your tasks: Harmonize RNA-seq datasets from multiple cohorts and age groups and develop an end-to-end subtype-discovery workflow, including quality control, batch correction, feature selection, manifold learning, subtype definition and stability assessment Build calibrated hierarchical machine-learning models that transfer subtype assignments across cohorts and platforms Evaluate subtype definitions in relation to molecular genetic findings, WHO/ICC and ELN categories, age, treatment, drug response and clinical outcomes Map AML subtypes onto atlases of hematopoietic development, assess their stemness states and validate bulk-derived findings using large-scale single-cell RNA-seq datasets Implement and document the best-performing methods in a reproducible R package and contribute to collaborative analyses, manuscripts, presentations and project reporting Your profile: We are looking for an enthusiastic doctoral researcher with a degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in bioinformatics, computational biology, data science, systems biology, molecular biology or a related quantitative or life-science discipline Programming skills in R and/or Python and a solid foundation in statistics or machine learning are required; willingness to work extensively in R is essential Experience with bulk or single-cell items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Interactive and Immersive Simulation of Animal Navigation in the Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group
items.desc: Paygrade E13 TV-L Working Hours 100% (suitable for part-time) Institution Institute of Physics (School of Mathematics and Natural Sciences) Location Oldenburg (Oldb) Application Deadline 30.10.2026 First day of work 01.01.2027 Limited for 3 years About us The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group at the University of Oldenburg invites applications for a three-year doctoral research position at the interface of computer science, physics, and biology. The project investigates how interactive and immersive simulation can help scientists explore, experiment with, and reason about computational models of animal navigation. Animals navigate using multiple environmental and sensory cues. Computational models allow researchers to investigate possible mechanisms, test hypotheses, and predict movement patterns. This PhD will develop and scientifically evaluate interactive approaches that make such models more accessible to systematic exploration, comparison, and interpretation. Virtual and mixed reality are promising approaches, alongside conventional desktop and potentially web-based interfaces. Research questions How can researchers interactively vary model parameters, assumptions, sensory cues, and competing navigation hypotheses? Under which conditions do immersive interfaces (VR/MR) offer advantages over conventional interfaces for exploring complex navigation simulations? How can interactive representations help connect individual simulated decisions and trajectories with population-level or large-scale movement patterns? How can the scientific value of different interaction techniques be evaluated in realistic research tasks? Your tasks Develop a research framework for visualizing and interacting with computational models of animal navigation. Design and implement methods to explore parameters, manipulate assumptions, compare hypotheses, and inspect simulated outcomes. Integrate existing or newly developed navigation models and simulation data into interactive environments, potentially using Unity, Unreal Engine, or other appropriate technologies. Design and conduct evaluations with researchers to assess how different interfaces support scientific exploration, interpretation, and reasoning. Collaborate closely with scientists in physics, biology, and computer science; document and disseminate results through scientific publications and presentations. Pursue an independent doctoral research project leading to a PhD. Your profile Required qualifications: Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Physics, Computational Biology, Engineering, Human–Computer Interaction, or a closely related discipline. Strong programming skills, for example in Python, C++, C#, or comparable languages. Experience in interactive software development, simulation, scientific computing, visualization, or related areas. Interest in computational modelling and in investigating scientific questions through software and empirical evaluation. Excellent written and spoken English; ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team. Advanced experience with machine learning methods Desirable qualifications Experience with VR/MR, Unity or Unreal Engine, 3D interaction, or immersive visualization. Knowledge of human–computer interaction, user studies, usability evaluation, or visual analytics. Experience with agent-based modelling, animal movement, navigation, ecological simulation, or trajectory analysis. Familiarity with reproducible research software, data pipelines, or scientific visualization. Possible additional application: science communication Methods developed for scientific research may also be adapted into accessible interactive demonstrations for public outreach, for example through VR/MR or web-based experiences at science events. This is a secondary opportunity rather than a separate educational-software development objective. We offer The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group (www.quantbiolab.com) develops computational approaches to biological and physical systems and works in an international, interdisciplinary research environment. The position offers collaboration across disciplines, access to modern computational and immersive-visualization infrastructure, doctoral supervision, and opportunities for scientific publication and professional development. Employment conditions and benefits follow the applicable collective agreement (TV-L) and university policies, including annual leave, flexible working arrangements, and university health and sports programmes. Our standards The University of Oldenburg is dedicated to increase the percentage of female employees in the field of science. Therefore, female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. In accordance to § 21 Section 3 NHG, female candidates with equal qualifications will be preferentially considered. Applicants with disabilities will be given preference in case of equal qualification. Apply now Please send your application via e-mail by 30.10.2026 to ilia.solovyov@uni-oldenburg.de Please submit a single PDF with the following reference number QBL10 containing a cover letter explaining your research motivation and relevant experience, a CV, academic transcripts, a brief statement of research interests, a list of publications or software projects (if applicable), and contact details of at least two referees. Applications should be sent to Prof. Dr. Ilia Solov’yov. The application deadline and anticipated starting date will be announced in the final advertisement. Benefits at University of Oldenburg 30 days vacation Secure remuneration according to collective agreement Company pension scheme Further education opportunities Flexible working hours Health management Remote working Compatibility of career and family Support with childcare University Sports Centre Certificate Bicycle-friendly employer Corporate Benefits

items.title: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators
items.desc: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators Help determine operational limits of next-gen nuclear steam generators! Job description Advanced nuclear reactor designs like the high temperature gas cooled reactor or molten salt reactor offer certain advantages compared to traditional light water reactors. One such advantage is their potential to operate with a high thermal efficiency. This advantage stems from the fact that these reactors operate at much higher temperatures, enabling superheated steam generation. Traditional light water reactors utilize so-called U-tube steam generators in which saturated steam is produced. It is well known that such steam generators suffer from spontaneous oscillations of two-phase mass flow and pressure drop on the shell side. This phenomenon is well understood in light water reactors, allowing for safe and stable operation. However, these boiling instabilities are more severe in once-through helical steam generators, as the dryout point will shift rapidly up and down along the helical tubes. This oscillating behaviour can lead to thermal fatigue of the tube walls, which can ultimately result in mechanical failure. While this phenomenon is already complex enough in and of itself, it typically coincides with parallel channel instabilities. In this project, you will develop and build a laboratory steam generator set-up to study boiling instabilities in helical tubes. In the first year, you will help design and build the set-up along with a team of skilled technicians and an energetic supervisory team. Subsequently, you will study the characteristics of the boiling instabilities within the set-up and compare them to a numerical model. Your Working Environment You will join the Process & Energy (P&E) department at TU Delft’s Mechanical Engineering faculty.Our department works along the themes of Energy, Flow and Processes. You will work together with top researchers highly skilled in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics. Moreover, we collaborate with researchers from the Reactor Institute Delft. You will have opportunities for professional development through both technical and non-technical courses. We expect that as part of your PhD you will take the lead on interacting and collaborating with other researchers at TU Delft, with research groups at other universities, and with industry and other stakeholders. Job requirements We are looking for a candidate with 1) ample experience in experimental techniques and design of experiments involving physical transport phenomena. Furthermore, we expect that you have 2) A MSc. degree in either chemistry, physics or mechanical engineering or similar field. 3) Strong affinity with thermodynamics and transport equations. 4) A keen interest in the nuclear industry and its future roles in society. 5) An interest in transient modelling and analysis. 6) Good communication skills and the ability to be a team player in a highly multidisciplinary setting. For this vacancy, a knowledge embargo exemption is required. Please check the following website: https://www.government.nl/themes/education/secondary-vocational-education-mbo-and-tertiary-higher-education/exemption-certain-engineering-or-nuclear-related-courses-of-study TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. . Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information about this vacancy, please contact dr. ir. Jurriaan Peeters (j.w.r.peeters@tudelft.nl). Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 15 November 2026 upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter You can address your application to dr. ir. Jurriaan Peeters. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Applying for an exemption for specific research and educational areas is an obligatory part of the selection procedure for this vacancy. This exemption must be obtained from the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (OCW) before an employment contract is agreed upon. . Please do not contact us for unsolicited services Faculty/Department: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering Salary range: €3204 - €4051 Hours per week: 36-40 FTE: 1,0 Submission is possible until: 15 Nov 2026 ID job: 3937

items.title: PhD in Machine Learning for Quantum Systems (1.0 FTE)
items.desc: Vacature ID: 16972 Functie categorie: PhD-posities Aanstellingsomvang in uren min: 38 Aanstellingsomvang in uren max: 38 Standplaats: Leiden Solliciteren kan tot en met: 30 november 2026 Teaser Text We are looking for PhD candidates interested in research at the intersection of machine learning (ML) and quantum many-body physics. The successful candidate will join Interpretable Machines for Physics (IMP) , a research group led by Dr. Anna Dawid. They will work on the mechanics of ML and developing new ML approaches to challenging quantum problems, with a strong focus on making these approaches interpretable, reliable, and scalable. In this position, you will learn about state-of-the-art deep learning solutions as well as the challenges of understanding neural networks. You will be given increasing scientific freedom, supported by structured mentoring, including career development plans guided by your plans after the PhD. The starting date is flexible, the latest in November 2027. The position is set in the exciting, friendly, and interdisciplinary environment of the aQa (Applied Quantum Algorithms) group, which is a team of faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and students across the Leiden Institute of Physics (LION), the Leiden Institute for Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), the Leiden Institute for Chemistry (LIC), and the Leiden Mathematical Institute (MI) at the Leiden University. What you will do Conducting research on the mechanics of deep learning and applications of (interpretable, reliable, and scalable) ML in quantum sciences with scientific integrity and rigor under the supervision of Dr. Anna Dawid; Assisting in relevant teaching activities; Actively participating in regular group and one-on-one meetings; Co-supervising Bachelor and Master students; Co-organizing scientific events; Presenting your research results to the scientific community at international conferences and through publications. Where you will work The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The faculty is home to more than 2,700 staff members and over 6,000 students enrolled in nine bachelor's and fifteen master's programs. We are located at the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry come together. You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. According to an independent research assessment, LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. We offer a clear and welcoming career path for young and talented scientists with the ambition to grow. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science What you bring Master’s degree in physics, computer science, or a closely related field; Strong interest in ML and motivation to make it interpretable and reliable; Knowledge of quantum physics and numerical methods for quantum systems or theory of deep learning is preferred; Good programming skills in Python; Proficient in spoken and written English; A team player who can communicate well across scientific fields and teams; Highly motivated and organized self-starter with an open mindset. What we offer An full-time employment contract for the duration of initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility the appointment will be extended by a further three years. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities; A salary between € 3.204,= and € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P); A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week. Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop. What we value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area and position details can be made to Dr. Anna Dawid ( a.m.dawid@liacs.leidenuniv.nl ). If you have any questions about the procedure, please sent an e-mail to: jobs@liacs.leidenuniv.nl . Applications: Please submit your application online via the blue button in the vacancy. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents: A CV that includes names and email addresses of at least two scientists who agreed to be contacted for reference letters; A short motivation letter (1 page); Optionally, a short research statement (1 page) describing your research projects so far and what research project you would be interested in doing during your PhD. For full consideration, please apply no later than 30 November 2026 . The selection procedure will take place in December/January 2027, and selected candidates may be invited for an interview during this period. items.title: PhD Position Flexibility in Nuclear Power
items.desc: PhD Position Flexibility in Nuclear Power Can nuclear- and renewable energy play nice? Job description Both Europe and the Netherlands are committed to transitioning to a CO2-neutral economy by 2050. As part of this commitment, the Netherlands has built large-scale wind park, and a significant amount of energy comes from solar power as well. While wind and solar energy help to decarbonize power generation, it also comes at a cost. Due to the intermittent availability of wind and solar energy, grid congestion can occur (which means that the grid lacks sufficient capacity to handle demand or supply of electricity). Therefore, the grid must be carefully managed. In many countries, gas power plants help manage the grid. However, since natural gas counteracts decarbonization, the question arises: “which other technologies can help reduce grid congestion? Small modular reactors (SMR) - nuclear reactors below 300 MWe – may be able to operate flexibly to help counteract grid congestion. As such reactors have less inertia, they are better suited to load-following than large-scale nuclear power plants. Even so, their ramp rates are much lower than other technologies. Through smart design of the power cycle and the inclusion of thermal energy storage, ramp rates of SMR’s can be greatly enhanced. In this thesis project, you will design advanced power cycles with or without energy storage for SMR’s to enable enhanced load-following. Using numerical techniques, you will couple transient power cycle modelling with nuclear reactor modelling to analyse any feedback to the reactor. You will run different load-following scenarios to ascertain technologically feasible enhanced ramp rates. You will be assisted by an expert supervisory team during your PhD. As the Dutch Nuclear industry is growing rapidly, and the Dutch Government has announced a significant expansion of nuclear energy, your results may actively contribute to shaping the Dutch nuclear landscape. Your Working Environment You will join the Process & Energy (P&E) department at TU Delft’s Mechanical Engineering faculty.Our department works along the themes of Energy, Flow and Processes. You will work together with top researchers highly skilled in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics. Moreover, we collaborate with researchers from the Reactor Institute Delft. You will have opportunities for professional development through both technical and non-technical courses. We expect that as part of your PhD you will take the lead on interacting and collaborating with other researchers at TU Delft, with research groups at other universities, and with industry and other stakeholders. Job requirements We are looking for a candidate with 1) ample experience in thermodynamic system modelling, in particular transient modelling; for example, heat pumps or power cycles. Any interest in nuclear is a plus. Furthermore, we expect that you have 2) A MSc. degree in either physics or mechanical engineering or similar field. 3) Strong affinity with thermodynamics and transport equations. 4) A keen interest in the nuclear industry and its future roles in society. 5) Keen interest in transient modelling and analysis. 6) Good communication skills and the ability to be a team player in a highly multidisciplinary setting.
