items.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
items.desc: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos: Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants should submit a dossier including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián.

items.title: PhD: "AI‑Infotainment Testing"(SEAT S.A. & UPC)
items.desc: Ever wondered what it’s like to work for an international company like SEAT & CUPRA? 🚀 If you are looking to take the next step in your professional career, our recent Industrial PhD project in collaboration with the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya might be exactly what you’re looking for. About The Project The automotive industry is entering a new era defined by software‑defined vehicles, advanced connectivity and increasingly complex digital ecosystems. Among them, Infotainment stands out as one of the most sophisticated and customer‑visible domains, combining HMI, apps, connectivity, vehicle signals, market variants and thousands of user scenarios. This complexity demands a new generation of intelligent validation systems. To address this challenge, we are launching an ambitious PhD project focused on developing an AI‑assisted validation ecosystem for CUPRA Infotainment — an intelligent super‑agent capable of transforming how we test, analyze and improve digital vehicle experiences. The aim of this PhD is to develop an advanced AI‑based framework capable of: Executing and improving Infotainment test cases autonomously Interacting with HMI screens, vehicle signals, buses, test benches and validation tools Detecting unexpected behavior beyond predefined specifications Pre‑analyzing failed tests and generating automated issue reports Learning from human feedback to increase reliability Proposing new tests based on documentation, defects, field claims and customer feedback Producing automated status reports and insights Exploring hybrid cloud‑edge execution for real‑time validation The Project Contributes To Improving Validation efficiency and coverage Early detection of customer‑impacting issues Internal AI capabilities Test prioritization based on real data Release recommendations Customer experience in a key digital vehicle domain What do we offer? Possibility to carry out a strategic and research project Access to a leading company in the automotive sector Be part of the Doctorate collective of the company Full-time 8:00h-16.35h(flexible schedule) Temporary contract for 3 years Required Qualifications Degree in Computer Engineering, Telecommunications, or Artificial Intelligence Master’s degree in Informatics Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or related fields Average academic score higher than 6.5 Advanced Spanish and English Valuable Experience Software engineering, data science or AI Python, C++, GenAI, AI agents, ML, data engineering, software testing Knowledge or interest in automation and automotive systems Key Competencies Analytical and critical thinking Strong research mindset Problem-solving skills Autonomy and responsibility Ability to explain technical concepts clearly At SEAT, we firmly believe in the power of diversity and inclusion as fundamental pillars of our culture, where everyone can be authentically free and freely authentic. We work with passion to create an environment in which every voice is heard and valued, ensuring equal opportunities for all people, regardless of sexual characteristics, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, nationality, ethnicity, cultural identity, age, beliefs, or any other form of diversity. Our commitment to diversity and inclusion is a priority that we hold ourselves accountable for every single day. Join us and become part of our team! #SEAT (PhD)

items.title: Doktorand i maskinkonstruktion
items.desc: Vill du vara med och bidra till framtidens autonoma system som överträffar människors förmågor? Du kommer att tillhöra forskningsämnet maskinkonstruktion på avdelning produkt- och produktionsutveckling som tillhör institutionen för teknikvetenskap och matematik. Här bedrivs forskning inom produktutveckling, simuleringsdriven konstruktion, automation av arbetsmaskiner samt modellering & simulering. Forskargruppen består av fyra seniorer samt sex doktorander och har tillgång till relevant forskningsinfrastruktur. Forskargruppen samverkar även med andra universitet, institut och företag både nationellt och internationellt. Ämnesbeskrivning Maskinkonstruktion omfattar, för tekniska system, simuleringsdriven produktutveckling, modellering och simulering, produktutvecklingsmetodik samt produktinformationshantering. Modeller, metoder, processer och verktyg för utveckling av produkter är centrala för ämnet. Projektbeskrivning Doktorandprojektet syftar till att utveckla metoder och en modulär systemarkitektur för säker samverkan mellan autonoma terränggående arbetsmaskiner. Forskningen omfattar hur övergripande uppdrag kan brytas ned till prioriterade och samordnade maskinuppgifter, exempelvis navigering, materialhantering och inspektion. Särskilt fokus läggs på hur uppgifter kan omplaneras när omgivningen, maskinernas tillstånd eller kommunikationsförutsättningarna förändras. Projektet ska även utveckla säkerhetsfunktioner som upptäcker människor, hinder, kollisionsrisker och systemfel samt aktiverar lämpliga åtgärder, såsom omplanering, hastighetsbegränsning eller säkert stopp. Metoderna integreras i en gemensam arkitektur för planering, perception, styrning, kommunikation och säkerhet. Resultaten ska bidra till användbara metoder för kostnadseffektiv utveckling och validering av robusta, säkra och samverkande autonoma arbetsmaskiner. Arbetsuppgifter En doktorandtjänst innebär både teoretiskt och praktiskt arbete. Som doktorand tränas du i vetenskapligt arbete i form av publicering av vetenskapliga artiklar i tidskrifter och vid nationella och internationella konferenser. Du läser även obligatoriska och frivilliga doktorandkurser. Dessutom kan du få möjlighet att prova på lärarrollen. Som forskare arbetar du som en neutral part i många sammanhang vilket ger en fantastisk möjlighet att lära sig att driva utmanande utvecklingsprojekt. Arbetet kommer mer specifikt att innefatta utveckling av olika autonoma dellösningar (framförallt mjukvarumässiga) som implementeras, testas och demonstreras med hjälp av terrängfordonsforskningsplattformen AORO. Kvalifikationer Universitetsexamen (MSc eller motsvarande) inom maskinteknik, robotik, produktionsteknik eller dylikt. Du bör ha ett stort intresse, nyfikenhet och passion för forskning och vi värdesätter din personlighet och individuella egenskaper högt. Erfarenhet av arbete med kinematik, dynamik, programmering, säkerhet och CAD-modellering är meriterande. Kunskaper om AI-stödd automation är speciellt meriterande. Sökande måste behärska engelska i tal och skrift. Eftersom undervisning bedrivs inom maskinkonstruktion är det meriterande om du har erfarenhet av CAD. I utvärderingen av kandidater beaktas Luleå tekniska universitets medarbetarpolicy och jämställdhetsmål. För ytterligare information om doktorandutbildning inom maskinkonstruktion se studieplan för forskarutbildning inom teknisk fakultet. Information Anställning som doktorand är tidsbegränsad på 4 år, undervisning och annan institutionstjänstgöring kan tillkomma upp till 20 % av heltid. Tjänstgöringsort är Luleå och tänkt tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Att söka en anställning | Luleå tekniska universitet För ytterligare information är du välkommen att kontakta Professor Magnus Karlberg, 0920-49 2418, magnus.karlberg@ltu.se Fackliga kontaktpersoner Ansökan Vi ser helst att du söker befattningen via ansökningsknappen nedan där du bifogar personligt brev samt CV/meritförteckning och kopior av verifierade examensbevis. Var vänlig och märk din ansökan med referensnumret nedan. Både ansökan och examensbevis ska vara skrivna på svenska eller engelska. Sista ansökningsdag: 5 november, 2026 Referensnummer: 5393-2026

items.title: PhD Student in Machine Design
items.desc: Would you like to contribute to the autonomous systems of the future—systems capable of exceeding human capabilities? You will join the research subject Machine Design at the Division of Product and Production Development, which is part of the Department of Engineering Sciences and Mathematics. Our research covers product development, simulation-driven design, automation of mobile machinery and modelling and simulation. The research group consists of four senior researchers and six PhD students and has access to relevant research infrastructure. The group also collaborates with universities, research institutes and companies, both nationally and internationally. Subject Description Machine Design encompasses, for engineering systems, simulation-driven product development, modelling and simulation, product development methodology and product information management. Models, methods, processes and tools for developing products are important for the research subject. Project Description The PhD project aims to develop methods and a modular system architecture for safe collaboration between autonomous off-road mobile machines. The research will investigate how high-level missions can be decomposed into prioritised and coordinated machine tasks, such as navigation, material handling and inspection. Particular attention will be given to replanning tasks when environmental conditions, machine states or communication conditions change. The project will also develop safety functions that detect people, obstacles, collision risks and system faults, and initiate appropriate responses such as replanning, speed reduction or a safe stop. The methods will be integrated into a common architecture for planning, perception, control, communication and safety. The results will contribute to practical methods for the cost-effective development and validation of robust, safe and collaborative autonomous mobile machinery. Duties A PhD position involves both theoretical and practical work. As a PhD student, you will receive training in scientific research, including publishing articles in scientific journals and presenting your work at national and international conferences. You will also take compulsory and elective doctoral courses and may have the opportunity to gain teaching experience. As a researcher, you will act as an independent party in many contexts, providing an excellent opportunity to learn how to manage challenging development projects. More specifically, the work will include developing autonomous subsystems, primarily software-based solutions, that will be implemented, tested and demonstrated using the AORO off-road vehicle research platform. Qualifications Applicants must hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in mechanical engineering, robotics, production engineering or a related field. You should have a strong interest in, curiosity about and passion for research. We attach considerable importance to personal qualities and individual suitability. Experience in kinematics, dynamics, programming, safety and CAD modelling is considered an asset. Knowledge of AI-assisted automation is particularly advantageous. Applicants must be proficient in spoken and written English. As teaching is conducted within Machine Design, experience in CAD is also considered an asset. The evaluation of candidates will take into account Luleå University of Technology’s employee policy and gender-equality objectives. For further information about doctoral studies in Machine Design, please see the general syllabus for third-cycle studies at the Faculty of Science and Technology. Further information The PhD position is a fixed-term, four-year appointment. Teaching and other departmental duties may be added, corresponding to no more than 20% of full-time employment. The position is based in Luleå, and the intended starting date is subject to agreement. Applying for a job | Luleå tekniska universitet For further information, please contact Professor Magnus Karlberg, +46 920 49 24 18, magnus.karlberg@ltu.se. Union representatives In case of different interpretations of the English and Swedish versions of this announcement, the Swedish version takes precedence. Application We prefer that you apply for this position by clicking on the apply button below . The application should include a CV, personal letter and copies of verified diplomas from high school and universities. Mark your application with the reference number below. Your application, including diplomas, must be written in English or Swedish. Closing date for applications: 5 November, 2026 Reference number: 5393-2026

items.title: PhD in Machine Learning for Quantum Systems (1.0 FTE)- NL
items.desc: We are looking for PhD candidates interested in research at the intersection of machine learning (ML) and quantum many-body physics. The successful candidate will join Interpretable Machines for Physics (IMP) , a research group led by Dr. Anna Dawid. They will work on the mechanics of ML and developing new ML approaches to challenging quantum problems, with a strong focus on making these approaches interpretable, reliable, and scalable. In this position, you will learn about state-of-the-art deep learning solutions as well as the challenges of understanding neural networks. You will be given increasing scientific freedom, supported by structured mentoring, including career development plans guided by your plans after the PhD. The starting date is flexible, the latest in November 2027. The position is set in the exciting, friendly, and interdisciplinary environment of the aQa (Applied Quantum Algorithms) group, which is a team of faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and students across the Leiden Institute of Physics (LION), the Leiden Institute for Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), the Leiden Institute for Chemistry (LIC), and the Leiden Mathematical Institute (MI) at the Leiden University. What You Will Do Conducting research on the mechanics of deep learning and applications of (interpretable, reliable, and scalable) ML in quantum sciences with scientific integrity and rigor under the supervision of Dr. Anna Dawid; Assisting in relevant teaching activities; Actively participating in regular group and one-on-one meetings; Co-supervising Bachelor and Master students; Co-organizing scientific events; Presenting your research results to the scientific community at international conferences and through publications. Where you will work The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The faculty is home to more than 2,700 staff members and over 6,000 students enrolled in nine bachelor's and fifteen master's programs. We are located at the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry come together. You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. According to an independent research assessment, LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. We offer a clear and welcoming career path for young and talented scientists with the ambition to grow. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science What You Bring Master’s degree in physics, computer science, or a closely related field; Strong interest in ML and motivation to make it interpretable and reliable; Knowledge of quantum physics and numerical methods for quantum systems or theory of deep learning is preferred; Good programming skills in Python; Proficient in spoken and written English; A team player who can communicate well across scientific fields and teams; Highly motivated and organized self-starter with an open mindset. What We Offer An full-time employment contract for the duration of initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility the appointment will be extended by a further three years. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities; A salary between € 3.204,= and € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P); A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week. Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop. What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area and position details can be made to Dr. Anna Dawid (a.m.dawid@liacs.leidenuniv.nl). If you have any questions about the procedure, please sent an e-mail to: jobs@liacs.leidenuniv.nl. Applications: Please submit your application online via the blue button in the vacancy. items.title: PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN- NL
items.desc: The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers capable of redefining kinase drug discovery beyond the ATP paradigm, by developing the experimental and computational tools, modular assays and workflows needed to systematically target non-conserved regulatory interfaces, such as kinase dimerization and substrate-binding sites. Proof-of-concept will be demonstrated on three representative kinases: EGFR, BRAF and the understudied “dark” kinase LTK. ANA-KIN brings together 11 beneficiaries and 9 associated partners across Europe and the USA, including Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (coordinator), University of Crete, Goethe University Frankfurt, Saarland University, EPFL, CNRS, Pompeu Fabra University, VIB, KU Leuven, INSERM and Leiden University, together with industrial partners such as AstraZeneca, Novartis, Servier and Skylight Therapeutics. The network combines chemical biology, structural biophysics (single-molecule FRET, cryo-EM, nanodiscs), AI-driven drug design and cell biology in an integrated learn–design–test loop. Twelve Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will each pursue an individual research project, benefit from co-supervision across institutions and sectors, carry out two research secondments at partner organizations, and follow a structured network-wide training program covering scientific, transferable, open-science and entrepreneurial skills. In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network. The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model predictions using second-harmonic generation (SHG)-based conformational profiling. The project will be supervised by Prof. Gerard J.P. van Westen (Leiden University), with Prof. Ruslan Efremov and Dr. Joshua Salafsky as co-supervisors. What You Will Do Conduct original and novel research in deep learning, AI, and cheminformatics for kinase drug discovery; Develop, benchmark and openly share models, datasets and decision-support dashboards following FAIR and open-science principles; Collaborate closely with experimental and computational DCs in the network, and carry out two research secondments abroad (VIB and Skylight Therapeutics, Belgium); Publish and present scientific articles at international journals and conferences; Participate in the ANA-KIN network-wide training events, schools and outreach activities; Contribute to educational activities; Write a dissertation. What You Bring A MSc degree in Computer Science, AI, (Computational) Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, or a relevant related field; Good knowledge of and experience with machine learning and deep-learning techniques (e.g. PyTorch); Good knowledge of and experience with cheminformatics and/or computational chemistry (e.g. RDKit, molecular descriptors, docking); Interest in structural biology, protein kinases and drug discovery; affinity with peptide or biophysical data is an advantage; Highly motivated to both perform foundational research and apply the developed methods to real-world problems; creative, ‘making things work’ mentality, independent, and communicative team player; Willingness to travel and to carry out research secondments at partner institutions abroad; Excellent programming skills (preferably Python); Good academic writing skills and interest in participating in educational activities; Excellent proficiency in English (oral and written). MSCA eligibility criteria At the date of recruitment, candidates must not have been awarded a doctoral degree; Mobility rule: candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the date of recruitment. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account. Where you will work Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research Our institute is a center of excellence for multidisciplinary research on drug discovery and development. Leiden University consistently ranks within the top-20 world-wide within the subject-based QS Ranking in Pharmacology and Pharmacy. At LACDR, we develop innovative scientific concepts in fundamental and translational research underlying the discovery and optimization of drugs, and personalized medicines. We aim to optimize the route to novel drugs that are both efficacious and safe, and therefore our research focuses on drug discovery and safety, bio-therapeutics, and systems biomedicine and pharmacology. State-of-the-art expertise and infrastructures ensure that we are strategically positioned in (inter)national collaborations, thus further strengthening the development of novel concepts and their application in a clinical and industry environment. Computational Drug Discovery Research in this group, headed by Gerard van Westen, focusses on computational methods integrated in different parts of the drug discovery process. More specifically, topics include innovative treatments for cancer, kinase and GPCR drug discovery, proteochemometrics, selectivity and polypharmacology modeling, allosteric modulation, drug resistance modeling, de novo molecular design, and novel methods in the domain of machine learning. For more information see: http://www.cddl.nl Research at our faculty The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from artificial intelligence, computer science, mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and almost 6,000 students. We are located in the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry meet. For more information, see http://www.science.leidenuniv.nl. What We Offer We offer a full-time appointment for 48 months as a Doctoral Candidate within the MSCA Doctoral Network ANA-KIN, starting late 2026. The appointment is initially for one year; after a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for the remaining period. Salary ranges from € 3.204,- tot € 4.051,- gross per month (pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities). Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3%), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school. As an ANA-KIN Doctoral Candidate you will also follow the network’s training program, including summer schools, workshops and an industrial immersion workshop, and your progress will be monitored by a Thesis Advisory Committee including an independent mentor. What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area can be made to Prof. Gerard van Westen, gerard@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact Brigitte Kraakman, b.p.m.kraakman@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application online via the blue button below. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents quoting the vacancy number and “ANA-KIN DC10”: application letter (including a statement confirming that they meet the MSCA eligibility criteria) curriculum vitae a list of grades two references (who have agreed to be contacted) Only applications received no later than November 12th can be considered. The selection procedure will take place in November. Selected candidates may be invited for an interview in the last week of November / 1st week of December, during which you are kindly requested to be available. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this.

items.title: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’
items.desc: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’ 1,0 FTE position for 4 years. The PhD candidate will be appointed for a period of 15 months. The appointment will be extended to 4 years when progress and performance are good. A PhD training program is part of the agreement. Vacancy number: FAC/BW/26087 The Project Can you help make energy data usable without giving away sensitive information? The energy transition in the Netherlands urgently requires upgrading of the electricity grid, for instance to accommodate solar panels, wind turbines, and electric vehicles. To efficiently plan and manage these upgrades, stakeholders such as grid operators, municipalities and energy communities need to share detailed data about electricity consumption, generation and grid operation. This data sharing however is prevented by concerns on the competitively sensitive nature and privacy of data, as it reveals detailed information about households, buildings and operational assets. Synthetic data generated by generative AI-models offers a promising alternative, but preserving statistical, temporal, and physical characteristics of real energy data while protecting sensitive information are major challenges. We are offering a PhD position in the SHARE project that addresses these challenges. Research challenges As a PhD candidate, you will develop methods for adaptive privacy protection of energy data , combining differential privacy, empirical privacy attacks and privacy–utility optimisation. Your research is part of the Adaptive Privacy and Legal Compliance work package in the SHARE project. More specifically, your challenges are to: Investigate how temporal patterns, spatial information, rare events and other distinctive features contribute to re-identification and inference risk. You will work with metrics such as uniqueness, entropy, attack success rates and time-series-specific indicators. Implement and study attacks such as membership inference, reconstruction, re-identification and attribute inference to understand where information leakage occurs in both original and synthetic datasets. Investigate methods that allocate stronger protection to sensitive components and lighter perturbation to lower-risk components, thereby preserving as much analytical utility as possible. Formulate privacy protection as an optimisation problem balancing formal privacy guarantees against statistical, temporal and physical utility requirements for energy-system applications. Collaborate closely with researchers at Radboud University, who develop physics-informed generative models for synthetic energy data, and investigate approaches such as differentially private training and post-generation privacy calibration. Work closely with distribution system operator Alliander and other consortium partners to evaluate whether the developed methods provide meaningful protection while retaining the information required for practical energy-system applications. Ultimately contribute to an open-source privacy layer for the SHARE toolbox. Requirements You hold, or will soon obtain, an MSc degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related discipline. You should have: a strong background in privacy-enhancing technologies, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity or statistical modelling; strong programming skills, particularly in Python; preferably, some familiarity with deep generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models) and probabilistic modelling; good written and spoken English skills; knowledge of Dutch language preferred not mandatory. Salary The salary is determined in accordance with salary scale P of Appendix A of the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities and ranges from € 3.204,-- gross per month upon commencement to € 4.051,-- gross per month in the fourth and final year, in case of full employment. The Open Universiteit provides good secondary benefits such as training, mobility, part-time employment and paid parental leave. Station The position is officially based in Heerlen. As part of the PhD project, you will mainly work at Radboud University in Nijmegen, where you will collaborate closely with the other researchers in the SHARE project. This setup enables close day-to-day collaboration with researchers working on machine learning, synthetic data and energy systems. You will be employed by Open Universiteit and supervised by Dr. Mina Alishahi as your primary supervisor, with Prof. dr. ir. Harald Vranken as co-supervisor. Information For more information about this vacancy you can contact: harald.vranken@ou.nl. Procedure Please apply to this position by sending an email to solliciteren@ou.nl, stating the vacancy number and including: your CV; a motivation letter; your MSc thesis or another representative piece of academic work, if available; contact details of two references. In your motivation letter, please briefly address the following three questions: Why are you interested in privacy-preserving machine learning and, in particular, this PhD project? Describe a research, thesis or programming project in which you worked with machine learning, privacy, cybersecurity, generative models or complex data. What was your own contribution? Provide a one-paragraph description of your MSc thesis, written for a reader outside your field. You will preferably start your employment on January 1st, 2027. Closing date: November 1st, 2026 Working at the Open University Working at the Open University means contributing to academic education for the most motivated students in the Netherlands and Flanders, as well as to scientific research with visible impact for people and society. With a broad range of bachelor’s and master’s programmes and short courses, the Open University makes lifelong learning accessible to everyone. There are no prior education requirements for bachelor’s programmes: anyone aged eighteen or older can enrol. Education is hybrid and flexible, available anytime and anywhere, at a pace that suits the student. The majority of the nearly 16,000 students combine their studies with work. This creates a valuable interaction: experiences and questions from professional practice enrich education and research and increase their societal relevance. It is therefore no coincidence that the Open University has ranked in the top three of the Dutch Keuzegids for universities for many years, and this year holds the number one position. In research, the university focuses on three central themes: healthcare, digitalisation and AI, and society and citizenship. Solutions to today’s challenges are sought across disciplinary boundaries and in collaboration with partners. The Open University employs approximately 800 staff members, has its main campus in Heerlen, and operates study centres in the Netherlands and Flanders. Its culture is people-centred, collaborative, and inclusive: an environment in which students, staff, and partners feel connected, with ample opportunities for personal development and a healthy work–life balance. Department of Computer Science You will be appointed within the Department of Computer Science of the Faculty of Science. The department’s research program “Towards high-quality and intelligent software” (2020–2025) consists of four research lines, focusing on: Techniques for quality assurance of software systems Software and computer system security, and privacy-by-design Responsible artificial intelligence, including methods and applications of AI Educational tools and computing education.

items.title: Promotion – State of Health (SoH) von Elektronik
items.desc: Unternehmensbeschreibung Bei Bosch gestalten wir Zukunft mit hochwertigen Technologien und Dienstleistungen, die Begeisterung wecken und das Leben der Menschen verbessern. Unser Versprechen an unsere Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter steht dabei felsenfest: Wir wachsen gemeinsam, haben Freude an unserer Arbeit und inspirieren uns gegenseitig. Willkommen bei Bosch. Die Robert Bosch GmbH freut sich auf deine Bewerbung! Stellenbeschreibung Du arbeitest an einem innovativen KI-basierten SoH-Konzept, das die verbleibende Nutzungsdauer von Batteriesystemen prognostiziert und nachhaltige Entscheidungen für Wiederverwendung, Reparatur und Recycling ermöglicht. Darüber hinaus entwickelst du eine umfassende Produktentscheidungsmatrix, die wirtschaftliche, technische und designbezogene Kriterien systematisch zusammenführt. Mit geeigneten Methoden, wie der hybriden Modellierung, bewertest du das von dir entwickelte SoH-Konzept und stellst dessen Praxistauglichkeit sicher. Nicht zuletzt wendest du deine Erkenntnisse auf ein Fokusprodukt an und integrierst Inspektionsdaten aus der Produktion (SPI, AOI, AXI), 0‑km‑Ausfalldaten, Zuverlässigkeitsdaten sowie Feldbelastungen. Qualifikationen Ausbildung: sehr guter Masterabschluss in Mikrosystemtechnik, Mikroelektronik, Physik oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang Erfahrungen und Know-how: praktische Erfahrungen im Bereich der datenbasierten Modellierung (z. B. hybride Modellierung, vorausschauende Wartung / Predictive Maintenance, Anomalieerkennung) Programmierkenntnisse in Python und relevanten Bibliotheken (z. B. PyTorch) Expertise im Bereich der Zuverlässigkeit (Lebensdauer, Ausfallmechanismen, Prüfung / Testing) von Elektronik Persönlichkeit und Arbeitsweise: du zeichnest dich durch ein starkes Interesse an technischer Nachhaltigkeit aus, insbesondere an der Verlängerung der Produktlebensdauer und der Schonung von Ressourcen; zudem bringst du ausgeprägte analytische und kommunikative Fähigkeiten mit; deine hohe wissenschaftliche Neugier treibt dich an, komplexe technische Zusammenhänge zu durchdringen und innovative Lösungsansätze zu entwickeln Begeisterung: du begeisterst dich für Nachhaltigkeit und datenbasierte Modellierung Sprachen: sehr gutes Deutsch und Englisch in Wort und Schrift Zusätzliche Informationen https://www.bosch-ai.com www.bosch.com/research Die finale Vergabe des Promotionsthemas obliegt deiner Hochschule als zentrale Anlaufstelle für deine Promotion. Beginn: nach Absprache Bitte sende uns deine aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (inkl. Lebenslauf und Zeugnissen) zu. Vielfalt und Inklusion sind für uns keine Trends, sondern fest verankert in unserer Unternehmenskultur. Daher freuen wir uns über alle Bewerbungen: unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Behinderung, Religion, ethnischer Herkunft oder sexueller Identität. Du hast Fragen zum Bewerbungsprozess? Celina Vanessa Dannecker (Personalabteilung) +49 711 811 21346 Du hast fachliche Fragen zum Job? Roumen Ratchev (Fachabteilung) +49 711 811 38509 Work beginnt hier: Jetzt bewerben!

items.title: PhD Student in Security and Privacy of Multi-Agent AI Systems
items.desc: Are you interested in doing research focused on ensuring the trustworthiness of emerging AI systems comprising multiple agents? Does it sound exciting to develop novel techniques for robust and privacy-preserving multi-agent collaboration? If so, you are welcome to apply for this position as a doctoral candidate. The project As AI agents start acting in groups, delegating, negotiating, and relying on each other's inputs and outputs, the security assumptions behind single-model systems stop holding. This project develops principled and scalable foundations for trustworthy collaboration between AI agents, sitting at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF) under a programme building research ties between Sweden and Taiwan, including opportunities for research visits among the participants. About Us RISE Research Institutes of Sweden AB is Sweden's research institute and innovation partner. In international collaboration with companies, academia, and the public sector, we contribute to a competitive business sector and a sustainable society. You will be part of the Cybersecurity unit at the department of Computer Science which is one of the largest technical cybersecurity groups in Sweden, conducting cutting-edge research on both fundamental and applied cybersecurity topics arising in AI, 6G, Internet of Things, etc. About The Role We are looking for a dedicated PhD student to strengthen our research in trustworthy multi-agent AI systems. Example research topics include evaluating the robustness of multi-agent systems under adversarial manipulation, designing secure and privacy-preserving multi-agent collaborative mechanisms, and verifiable decision-making under uncertainty and adversarial influence. You will be based in the RISE office at Kista, Stockholm for 4 years, and you will be enrolled as a doctoral student at a Swedish University. PhD education also involves participation in relevant university courses. Who are you? Requirements: Completed master’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, information security, mathematics, or an equivalent field (at the time of employment) Strong programming skills Good command of spoken and written English Passion for agentic AI and cybersecurity Interest in technical challenges and commitment to delivering high-quality results Meriting: Experience with research projects Demonstrated collaboration skills Demonstrated drive and independence Personal qualities: Driven by curiosity Takes initiative naturally Strong problem-solving abilities Passionate and self-motivated Employment Start date: As soon as possible or according to agreement. Salary: According to Swedish norm. Assessment Criteria: Selection for doctoral education is based on the assessed ability to benefit from doctoral education. Welcome with your application! If this sounds exciting and you want to know more, you are welcome to contact Dr. Apostolos Pyrgelis (apostolos.pyrgelis@ri.se). For further information, you can contact Prof. Shahid Raza (shahid.raza@ri.se) or the director of the RISE cybersecurity unit Andreas Aurelius (andreas.aurelius@ri.se). The deadline for applications is October 15, 2026 . Interviews will be carried out continuously during the application period. Apply as soon as possible with personal letter, cv, academic transcripts, a copy of degree diploma(s), and a copy of your passport/National ID card. Our union representatives Ingemar Petermann, SACO, +46 10 228 41 22, and Linda Ikatti, Unionen, 010-516 51 61.

items.title: CIFRE - Intégration d’architectures de qubits de spin en silicium en technologie CMOS FDSOI avancée pour le calcul quantique (F/H)
items.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. La course à la réalisation d’un ordinateur quantique démontrant la suprématie quantique s’intensifie, mobilisant de puissantes entreprises et de nombreux gouvernements, qui travaillent sur de multiples supports physiques pour encoder l’information quantique, tels que la supraconductivité, les ions piégés, le spin de l’électron dans le silicium ou encore la photonique. Au‑delà des enjeux économiques classiques, l’adoption de solutions quantiques est hautement stratégique, ouvrant la voie vers une sécurité renforcée des données et des communications. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans la feuille de route actuelle de ST, dans le cadre du contrat de collaboration avec QUOBLY, visant à produire industriellement un ordinateur quantique tolérant aux fautes (FTQC) pour des clients stratégiques. Dans cette compétition, ST et QUOBLY peuvent tirer parti de la technologie FDSOI, qui offre un environnement idéal pour isoler et manipuler le spin de l’électron utilisé dans les algorithmes quantiques. Pendant les 3 années de recherche, le doctorant devra étudier et proposer une architecture de dispositif basée sur la technologie CMOS FDSOI permettant de supporter des qubits en silicium à base de spin pour le calcul quantique. Les principaux axes de développement seront : l’architecture du dispositif (simulation 3D et réalisation des dispositifs sur silicium), l’analyse des matériaux et la caractérisation cryogénique. A propos de vos missions Réaliser une étude bibliographique exhaustive afin de situer au mieux le sujet et sa complexité. Développer des architectures de transistors à électron unique (SET) dans une technologie CMOS FDSOI avancée. Implémenter une architecture de qubit innovante (passage d’une structure linéaire 1D à une matrice 2D). Optimiser le layout des qubits en tirant parti des techniques de lithographie avancées utilisées dans les technologies FDSOI. Effectuer des simulations 3D, embarquer des structures de test et réaliser les dispositifs correspondants sur silicium. Caractériser les qubits et les SET en régime cryogénique Mener une caractérisation avancée des pièges dans les diélectriques à température ambiante et à basse température. A propos de vous Niveau Bac+5 (Master 2 ou diplôme d’ingénieur) en micro/nanoélectronique, physique des dispositifs, électronique ou physique quantique appliquée (ou formation équivalente). Bases solides en physique des semi-conducteurs, dispositifs MOSFET (FDSOI/FinFET) et compréhension d’une filière technologique CMOS. Expérience pratique en salle blanche, caractérisation électrique ou design de circuits/dispositifs appréciée. Bonnes capacités scientifiques (esprit critique, lecture d’articles) et compétences en programmation/outils numériques. Excellentes aptitudes en communication, anglais scientifique et travail en équipe interdisciplinaire. Les résultats attendus de cette recherche sont la conception, le développement et la compréhension des performances des nouvelles architectures des qubits et de SET intégrant des matériaux avancés, capables de satisfaire les exigences du calcul quantique. Contact: carlos-augusto.suarezsegovia@st.com ST est fière d’être certifiée parmi les 17 entreprises mondiales « Global Top Employers 2025 » et d’être la première et unique entreprise de semi-conducteurs à recevoir cette distinction. ST a été distinguée dans ce classement grâce à sa démarche d’amélioration continue, se démarquant notamment par son engagement en matière d’éthique et d’intégrité, de sens et de valeurs, d’organisation et de gestion du changement, ainsi que par sa stratégie commerciale et ses performances. En France, ST a également obtenu la labélisation Happy Trainee 2025. Nous cultivons un environnement de travail inclusif et diversifié, où la discrimination n’a pas sa place. Notre ambition est de recruter et de fidéliser des talents reflétant la richesse des sociétés dans lesquelles nous évoluons. Nous nous engageons à l’équité dans le développement des carrières, les opportunités professionnelles et la rémunération. Chez ST, nous encourageons les candidats qui ne remplissent pas forcément tous les critères à postuler, car nous croyons en la richesse des parcours variés et offrons de réelles opportunités d’apprentissage et d’évolution. La diversité, l’équité et l’inclusion sont des valeurs fondamentales qui façonnent notre culture d’entreprise. Pour découvrir toutes nos opportunités, rendez-vous sur st.com/careers.

items.title: Industridoktorand inom nätverkssäkerhet – Sectra Communications
items.desc: Vill du utveckla din expertis inom nätverkssäkerhet, framtida kryptografi och dataskydd samtidigt som du gör skillnad och bidrar till en säkrare värld? Sectra Communications är en ledande leverantör inom cybersäkerhet och informationssäkerhet. Här utvecklas lösningar inom kryptering och IT-säkerhet för att stärka samhällets säkerhet och skydda känslig information, både i Sverige och Europa. Forskningsavdelningen har som ansvar att utveckla kunskap, metoder och prototyper som banar väg för framtidens säkra kommunikationslösningar och cybersäkerhetsprodukter. Forskningsområdet för den här tjänsten berör skydd av nätverkskommunikation. Trots stark kryptering kan nätverkstrafik fortfarande röja känslig information genom mönster som paketstorlek, tidpunkt och frekvens, och i takt med utvecklingen inom AI blir sådana analysmetoder allt kraftfullare. Arbetet handlar om att utveckla, driftsätta och utvärdera prestandamedvetna försvar som anpassar sig efter både nätverksförhållanden och angripare, med målet att överbrygga gapet mellan forskning och praktiskt användbara lösningar för en säkrare kommunikation. Rollen I rollen som industridoktorand hos Sectra Communications kommer du att jobba i ett team med forskare och ha nära samarbete med akademiska experter globalt. Projektet utförs i särskilt samarbete med Karlstads universitet och Linköpings universitet. Vidare kommer du att: Delta i forskningsavdelningens interna projekt Arbeta i nära anslutning till våra utvecklingsavdelningar för att förverkliga forskningen Delta på konferenser för att presentera men även lyssna in på forskning Vid intresse finns även stora möjligheter till internationella resor och samarbeten. Att vara industridoktorand hos oss innebär att kombinera det bästa av två världar. Du får möjlighet att fördjupa dig i forskningsfronten och avancera inom ditt expertområde, samtidigt som du arbetar praktiskt med att omsätta forskningen i verkliga, användbara produkter. , Denna roll är en unik möjlighet som kräver engagemang och flexibilitet. Du behöver ha en positiv inställning till de utmaningar som forsknings- och industrivärlden erbjuder, och se detta som en väg till en belönande och utvecklande karriär. Vi lägger större vikt vid din potential än den kunskap och erfarenhet du besitter idag. Om du är en snabblärd person med en strävan att utvecklas kan vi lära dig det som krävs för tjänsten. För att lyckas i rollen ser vi att du har: En civilingenjörsexamen inom datavetenskap, teknisk fysik eller ett närliggande område. Flytande svenska och engelska i både tal och skrift. Ett starkt intresse för att omvandla avancerad teknologi till praktiska lösningar inom cybersäkerhet. Mycket goda akademiska resultat och en stark vilja att lära dig och behärska nya tekniska metoder. För denna tjänst behöver du ett svenskt medborgarskap då vi jobbar med säkerhetsklassad information. Vi erbjuder: Möjligheten att arbeta med teknologier som spelar en avgörande roll för samhällets säkerhet. Möjligheten att lära dig om, och driva framstegen inom, ett av de mest betydelsefulla teknikområdena i vår tid. En inspirerande och utmanande arbetsplats där du arbetar tillsammans med smarta och begåvade kollegor, både inom industrin och akademin. En organisation där du blir hörd och har en verklig möjlighet att påverka. Vi läser ansökningar löpande och kommer kalla in till intervjuer efter sommaren. Här kan du läsa mer om hur det är att jobba på Sectra, och här kan du läsa mer om vår rekryteringsprocess.

items.title: PhD Position Sustainable Generative AI for Digital Sovereignty
items.desc: Join us for this PhD project in EU Horizon €8 million initiative, to transform how generative AI is deployed across Europe for a more sustainable, sovereign and resilient future. Job Description Generative AI is widely expected to become a central element of digital transformation. Its flexibility and adaptability give businesses in many sectors an opportunity to innovate rapidly, respond to changing conditions, and lower barriers to automation. For society to benefit from these advancements, organisations need to maintain control over sensitive information and critical decision-making tools. Reducing dependence on external providers strengthens digital autonomy, while more efficient ways of running AI help align technological progress with environmental and energy targets. By designing systems that are sustainable, sovereign, secure, and efficient at the same time, this PhD project will support Europe’s broader ambitions for responsible technological leadership. Position Overview: This PhD position is aimed at candidates with a Master’s degree in computer science/engineering, AI, data science, or related fields, with a strong interest in generative AI. The successful candidate will be based at the Department of Engineering Systems and Services (ESS) at Delft University of Technology under the supervision of Dr. Aaron Ding, Dr. Marcela Tuler de Oliveira, Prof. Dr. Marijn Janssen. This PhD project involves close collaboration with partners from the EU Horizon project, and candidates will have the opportunity to engage with interdisciplinary teams involved in the project. Key Responsibilities: To conduct an in-depth evaluation of existing foundation models to assess their suitability in the digital industries, automotive and healthcare domains. Design sustainable inference strategies and framework towards the computing continuum. Collaborate with experts from the f-inference consortium to design, develop, test and refine the design strategies and framework. Work independently and contribute collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team environment. Project Impact: This project will democratise the access to advanced Generative AI technologies through practical tools that help businesses, particularly SMEs, adopt state-of-the-art AI models. The outcomes are expected to enhance competitiveness, support sustainable innovation, and contribute to a more inclusive digital transition across Europe. Job Requirements MSc in computer science/engineering, AI, data science, or related fields. Strong analytical skills A strong interest in interdisciplinary research, and the use of AI in inter-oranisational context Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a dynamic, multidisciplinary environment. Excellent command of English TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Technology, Policy & Management The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Aaron Ding (aaron.ding@tudelft.nl). For more information about the application procedure, please contact Olivie Beek, HR-advisor (recruitment-tbm@tudelft.nl). Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: your CV motivation letter official list of all courses followed during your BSc and MSc studies with grades your MSc thesis If the applicants are selected for an interview, they will be asked to provide contact details of two referees with their consent. The start date is flexible, but foreseen for summer/fall 2026. Screening starts as applications come in. You can address your application to Aaron Ding. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

items.co: Fraunhofer Institute for Production Technology IPT
items.title: Doktorand IT (m/w/d)
items.desc: Die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft (www.fraunhofer.de) ist eine der weltweit führenden Organisationen für anwendungsorientierte Forschung. 74 Institute entwickeln wegweisende Technologien für unsere Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft - genauer: 30 000 Menschen aus Technik, Wissenschaft, Verwaltung und IT. Am Fraunhofer-Institut für Produktionstechnologie IPT in Aachen gestalten wir mit mehr als 450 Mitarbeitenden die Produktion der Zukunft - digital, nachhaltig und resilient. In der Abteilung »Produktionsqualität und Messtechnik« trägst du maßgeblich dazu bei, innovative Hardware- und Softwarelösungen für die Produktion von morgen zu entwickeln. Dabei verbinden wir moderne Mess- und Sensortechnik mit Datenanalyse und Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) sowie Steuerungs- und Automatisierungstechnik. Die Einsatzgebiete reichen von der Qualitätssicherung und Prozessüberwachung bis hin zur intelligenten Steuerung und Optimierung komplexer Produktionsprozesse in unterschiedlichsten Branchen Dabei bildet die gezielte Erfassung und Verarbeitung von Mess- und Produktionsdaten die Grundlage für eine höhere Produktqualität, stabile Prozesse und eine effiziente Produktion. Aufgaben Entwicklung und Integration innovativer Mess- und Automatisierungslösungen für industrielle Produktionsprozesse Erarbeitung technischer Lösungsansätze in den Bereichen Sensorik, Systemsteuerung sowie Daten- und Signalverarbeitung Entwicklung von Hard- oder Software zur Erfassung, Verarbeitung, Vernetzung und Visualisierung von Mess- und Produktionsdaten Anwendung von Datenanalyse, Machine Learning und Künstlicher Intelligenz zur Prozessüberwachung, Qualitätssicherung und Optimierung Akquisition, Koordination und Bearbeitung von nationalen und internationalen Industrie- und Forschungsprojekten im Team Präsentation deiner Forschungsergebnisse bei Auftraggebern sowie auf internationalen Konferenzen und Fachtagungen Qualifikationsprofil Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master, Diplom) im Bereich Maschinenbau, Elektrotechnik, Automatisierungstechnik, Informatik, Physik oder in einer verwandten Fachrichtung Begeisterung für technische Systeme und innovative Technologien in der Produktion Interesse an einem oder mehreren Themenfeldern wie Sensorik, Datenanalyse, KI, Steuerungstechnik oder Automatisierung Gute Kenntnisse in einer oder mehreren Programmiersprachen, beispielsweise Python, C++, C# oder MATLAB, sind von Vorteil Gute analytische Fähigkeiten und Freude an interdisziplinärer Projektarbeit Eigeninitiative, Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Spaß an Teamwork Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Wir bieten Ein engagiertes Team mit offener, wertschätzender Arbeitskultur Verantwortungsvolle Aufgaben in hochinnovativen Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprojekten Enge Zusammenarbeit mit renommierten Industriepartnern aus unterschiedlichen Branchen Ein hochmoderner Maschinenpark mit Edge-Cloud-Technologien und 5G-Infrastruktur Flexible Arbeitszeiten und Unterstützung bei der Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Privatleben Individuelle Weiterbildungs- und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten Möglichkeit zur Promotion an der RWTH Aachen in einem selbst entwickelten Forschungsthema Ein exzellentes Netzwerk aus Wissenschaft und Industrie mit hervorragenden Karriereperspektiven Attraktive Zusatzleistungen wie Deutschlandticket-Zuschuss, Mitarbeitendenrabatte und attraktive Benefits Warum Fraunhofer IPT? Bei uns verbindest du wissenschaftliche Exzellenz mit praxisnaher Forschung. Du entwickelst Technologien, die unmittelbar in industriellen Anwendungen zum Einsatz kommen, übernimmst früh Verantwortung in Industrie- und Forschungsprojekten und schaffst gleichzeitig die Grundlage für deine wissenschaftliche Karriere - bis hin zur Promotion. Die nachhaltige Erhöhung des Anteils von Frauen in der Wissenschaft ist unser erklärtes Ziel. Mit unserem Karriereprogramm »Fraunhofer TALENTA« bieten wir Berufseinsteigerinnen und Young Professionals zusätzliche Qualifizierungs- und Vernetzungsangebote sowie den nötigen Freiraum zur Gestaltung ihres Karrierewegs. Wir wertschätzen und fördern die Vielfalt der Kompetenzen unserer Mitarbeitenden und begrüßen daher alle Bewerbungen - unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung sowie persönlicher Orientierung und Identität. Schwerbehinderte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt eingestellt. Die wöchentliche Arbeitszeit beträgt 39 Stunden. Die Stelle kann auch in Teilzeit besetzt werden. Die Stelle ist zunächst auf 2 Jahre befristet. Es besteht die Möglichkeit der Verlängerung. Anstellung, Vergütung und Sozialleistungen basieren auf dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TVöD). Zusätzlich kann Fraunhofer leistungs- und erfolgsabhängige variable Vergütungsbestandteile gewähren. Bereit für Veränderung? Dann bewirb Dich jetzt online und mache einen Unterschied!

items.title: CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship
items.desc: 🎓 PhD Opportunity | Artificial Intelligence in Childhood Leukaemia Research 🔬 Interested in using AI and data science to advance childhood cancer research? The Leukaemia Research Cytogenomics Group (LRCG) at Newcastle University is recruiting a PhD student through the Cancer Research UK (CRUK) Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship Programme, with applications now open for the 2027 intake. This exciting project will focus on developing and evaluating trustworthy synthetic healthcare data using statistical methods, machine learning and generative AI, drawing on a national dataset of more than 20,000 childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients. The research aims to support more robust, reproducible and privacy-conscious approaches to childhood leukaemia research, with the potential to improve our understanding of treatment pathways and patient outcomes. 🔬 Project focus: Developing and comparing statistical, machine-learning and generative AI approaches to synthetic healthcare data generation. Evaluating the preservation of clinically important patterns, treatment pathways and outcomes, including rare events such as relapse. Assessing data utility, privacy, fidelity, fairness and clinical validity. Exploring the use of synthetic data for methodological research, hypothesis generation and reproducible analysis. 🌍 What the scholarship offers: Fully funded 4-year PhD, including stipend and tuition fees (Home fee status). Mentoring and leadership development opportunities. Networking through Black in Cancer and the Windsor Fellowship. A supportive and diverse research environment. Opportunities for research placements and community engagement. 👩‍💻 Who should apply? We welcome applicants with backgrounds in statistics, data science, biostatistics, epidemiology, computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines. As part of the CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer Programme, we particularly encourage applications from talented Black students who are passionate about advancing cancer research and addressing inequalities in healthcare. 📍 Location: Newcastle University, UK 👨‍🏫 Primary Supervisor: Dr. Amir Enshaei 📅 Application deadline: 4 December 2026 🎓 Start: 2027 intake 🔗 Find out more and apply: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/cancer/training/studentships/cruk-black-leaders-phd/ For informal enquiries, please contact Amir Enshaei (Primary Supervisor). Join us in advancing AI-driven research to improve outcomes for children with leukaemia! #PhDOpportunity #PhDStudentship #BlackLeadersInCancer #CancerResearch #ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning #DataScience #ChildhoodLeukaemia #SyntheticData #NewcastleUniversity
