items.title: PhD Position 100% – AI Literacy & Regulatory Learning (m/w/d)
items.desc: Your tasks Examine how AI-literacy frameworks cultivate individual and organisational absorptive capacity in public bodies and support regulatory learning. Use case studies and pre/post assessments to measure how literacy interventions affect evidence generation, procurement choices, escalation paths and the circulation of lessons across units and agencies. Build an inventory and typology of AI-literacy frameworks, validate interventions, report on literacy effects, and develop guidance for integrating literacy with procurement and review cycles. Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team; prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials; complete a doctoral thesis and related publications. Participate in REGULAIRE training, network reviews, dissemination, practitioner engagement, summer schools and monthly paper development seminars. Secondment Within the position, a secondment to a partner organization is planned. Supervision Primary supervision by Prof. Aurelia Tamò-Larrieux (HSG), co-supervision by Ass. Prof. Sandra Cortesi, plus a sectoral mentor at the secondment host. The secondment provides direct insight into the design and evaluation of AI-literacy initiatives in a public administration. Your profile Master's degree (or equivalent qualification giving access to doctoral studies at the University of St. Gallen) in public administration, political science, learning sciences, information systems, communication, law, or a related social science/interdisciplinary field, completed by the start date. Skills or demonstrable interest in case studies and intervention research, including pre/post assessment designs. Strong interest in AI literacy, public administration, AI governance and interdisciplinary research. Excellent written and spoken English; reliable, independent and analytical working style. Willingness to engage in international mobility and network-wide activities, including the planned secondment. Fulfilment of the doctoral admission requirements of the University of St.Gallen and the MSCA eligibility conditions. Eligibility Applicants may be of any nationality and must not hold a doctoral degree at the start of MSCA employment. Applicants must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: they must not have resided or carried out their main activity in Switzerland for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date (subject to the standard MSCA exclusions). Applicants must be eligible for timely enrolment in the relevant doctoral programme at the University of St.Gallen. The Institute of Law and Economics (ILE-HSG) conducts research at the interface of law (tax law and public law) and business (corporate governance, reporting and tax & trade). www.ile.unisg.ch . We offer A doctoral position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network REGULAIRE, with an international cohort of 15 doctoral candidates across ten European universities. Cross-institutional supervision, network-wide methods training, three residential summer schools, monthly paper development seminars and practitioner engagement. A stimulating interdisciplinary research environment at the University of St.Gallen with opportunities to contribute to national and international research and policy networks. A planned three-month intersectoral secondment as part of the doctoral project. The opportunity to complete a doctoral thesis and develop an independent research profile in AI governance, law and technology, and regulatory learning. Documents Motivation letter; CV; academic credentials/transcripts; at least two reference letters; a short research proposal engaging with the doctoral project. Apply Apply on the portal of the University of St. Gallen Application Deadline 07.11.2026 We are looking forward to your online-application stating the job ID apply here Inspirational Work Environment At the HSG, as Europe's leading business university, we operate in an entrepreneurial environment where you will meet highly qualified, ambitious experts - both regionally and internationally. For example, you benefit from a modern IT infrastructure and, in our library via HSGswisscovery, from nationwide access to the wealth of scientific information available. Executive Education We support internal and external executive education opportunities. Our internal executive education programme offers you a practical, dedicated and didactically mature transfer of knowledge in the form of seminars, e-learning, coaching and collegial advice. We support task-specific external training and executive education financially as well as with regard to the time required. Network We promote our culture of cross-functional collaboration and create space for forging valuable relationships - also with external partners. Regular exchanges and internal events help to strengthen these relationships and make them long-lasting. Family & Career We provide our employees with flexible work time models with a variable number of hours per week. As a family-friendly employer, we offer part-time positions, 16 weeks of maternity leave and a subsidised crèche, as well as support with childcare during the vacations. Equal Opportunities The University enables equal opportunities for all employees and students. This applies to degree courses and work, as well as academic careers, university management positions and the reconciliation of studies, work and private commitments. We are committed to this with various measures in the areas of teaching, research, administration and the Presidency. Fit and Healthy We help you stay fit and healthy. In addition to our diverse range of sports activities at the university, most of which are free of charge, and campaign weeks for corporate health management, we also offer you fruit in the workplace. In our canteen you will find a wide selection of freshly prepared meals - from vegetarian to fish dishes - at discounted prices. Further information on working at the HSG can be found here. University of St.Gallen «A place where knowledge is created» - As one of Europe's leading universities of economics and business administration, the University of St.Gallen (HSG), Switzerland, is committed to the education of over 10'000 students. The HSG is one of the largest employers in the region and provides an attractive and innovative environment for more than 3'800 researchers, educators and professional staff.

items.title: Doktorandplats - statistiker inom tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården
items.desc: Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna. Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård ansvarar för delar av läkarprogrammet. Inom forskarutbildning har vi en egen forskarskola i allmänmedicin. Vår primärvårdsforskning omfattar varierande projekt kring multisjuklighet, folksjukdomar som diabetes, nedsatt njurfunktion och psykisk ohälsa samt även pedagogiska projekt. Närmare 100 personer, av vilka cirka 30 doktorander, är anknutna till avdelningen. Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet? Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid. Forskargruppen Doktorandtjänsten finns inom forskargruppen för STEADY-CAN (Stockholm Early Detection of Cancer Study) vid Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård, Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS). Gruppen består av kliniskt aktiva forskare, statistiker och doktorander som arbetar med tidig upptäckt av cancer, i nära samarbete med Regionalt cancercentrum Stockholm-Gotland och internationella samarbetspartners. Gruppen är involverad i flera pågående forskningsprojekt, inklusive utveckling av statistiska och maskininlärningsbaserade prediktionsmodeller, longitudinell analys av blodprovsdata och registerbaserade kohortstudier inom cancerepidemiologi. Du kommer att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig grupp där statistiker, allmänläkare och epidemiologer arbetar nära varandra. I praktiken innebär det att du regelbundet diskuterar analysval med kliniker, förklarar statistiska metoder för personer utan statistisk bakgrund och själv lär dig om den kliniska vardagen i primärvården. Gruppen har regelbundna gemensamma analysmöten där du förväntas både ge och ta emot återkoppling på pågående arbete. Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter Detta doktorandprojekt kombinerar traditionell statistisk modellering och maskininlärning i tillämpad forskning kring tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården. Projektet använder data från STEADY-CAN-kohorten, som omfattar över 2,7 miljoner vuxna i Region Stockholm med länkade laboratorie-, journal- och registerdata. Under doktorandutbildningen kommer kandidaten att få bred kunskap inom överlevnadsanalys, prediktionsmodellering, maskininlärning och hantering av stora registerbaserade datamängder. Vi söker en motiverad doktorand med god bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. Den framgångsrika kandidaten förväntas ta ett stort eget ansvar genom hela projektet, med stöd från handledarna. Detta innebär konstruktion av analysdatamängder, statistisk analys och implementering av maskininlärningsmetoder, författande av vetenskapliga artiklar samt deltagande i institutionens seminarier och i nationella och internationella konferenser. Vad erbjuder vi? En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård. Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger. Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.* Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. *Om du anser dig ha motsvarande kunskaper ska du följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Bedömning av motsvarande kunskaper för grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. B) Särskilt behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det särskilda behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: - Intygar kunskaper i engelska (motsvarande Engelska B/Engelska 6 vid gymnasiet med godkänt betyg). Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan English language requirements for doctoral education. Kontroll av dokument Karolinska Institutet gör kontroll av dokumenten för att upptäcka förfalskningar. Karolinska Institutet förbehåller sig rätten att återkalla antagningsbeslut om förfalskningar eller oriktigheter påvisas. Inlämnande av falska handlingar är ett brott mot svensk lag och anses vara grund för rättsliga åtgärder. Färdigheter och personliga egenskaper Den sökande bör ha en gedigen bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. En examen i statistik/biostatistik eller matematisk statistik på avancerad nivå, t.ex. en masterexamen, är starkt meriterande. Utmärkta kunskaper i biostatistik och praktisk erfarenhet av överlevnadsanalys är meriterande. Tidigare erfarenhet av databehandling och statistisk analys är meriterande. Dessa erfarenheter ska företrädesvis vara från en medicinsk forskningsmiljö. Mycket goda kunskaper i statistisk programmering, företrädesvis i R, är avgörande för rollen. Erfarenhet av arbete med svenska registerdata är meriterande. Ett starkt intresse för medicinsk forskning i kombination med en passion för att tillämpa statistiska metoder för att besvara kliniskt relevanta forskningsfrågor är mycket önskvärt. Då STEADY-CAN-databasen, inklusive journal- och registervariabler och tillhörande beskrivningar, är på svenska är goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift ett krav. Handledningen och det internationella samarbetet sker delvis på engelska, varför goda kunskaper även i engelska i tal och skrift också krävs. Den sökande ska ha god kommunikationsförmåga, vilket är avgörande för att samarbeta med tvärvetenskapliga team och effektivt presentera forskningsresultat. Vi lägger mycket stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper i denna rekrytering. Den idealiska kandidaten bör vara: Självständig, strukturerad och med stark analytisk förmåga. Flexibel och ivrig att lära. Denna roll innebär kontinuerligt lärande och anpassning till nya metoder och utmaningar. Öppen för konstruktiva synpunkter och förmåga att delta i balanserad, analytisk självreflektion. Kandidaten ska även trivas med att arbeta i team och samarbeta väl med teammedlemmar med olika akademisk bakgrund. Förklara i ditt personliga brev hur du uppfyller de nödvändiga färdigheterna och egenskaperna. Villkor Doktorandplatsen innebär en anställning som doktorand under maximalt 4 år på heltid. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen i rekryteringsverktyget Varbi. Använd knappen uppe till höger och följ anvisningarna. Vi ser gärna att din ansökan är skriven på engelska, men det går också bra att ansöka på svenska. Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
items.desc: Tecnun - Escuela de Ingeniería-Universidad de Navarra Tecnun-Escuela de Ingeniería , perteneciente a la Universidad de Navarra , se propone contribuir a la formación profesional, científica y humana de los futuros ingenieros. Desde su creación, en la primavera de 1961, mantiene un equilibrio entre la docencia, la investigación y el servicio a la sociedad, haciendo que estas actividades se complementen entre sí. Actualmente dispone de dos campus : la sede más antigua, ubicada en el campus universitario del Bº de Ibaeta, está integrada por los edificios de laboratorios, el edificio docente y de representación concluido en 1989, y un edificio multiuso, levantado en 1996. La otra sede se encuentra en el Parque Tecnológico de Miramón e integra las aulas y laboratorios de investigación de las áreas de Electricidad, Electrónica y Comunicaciones. Descripción de la oferta Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants Should Submit a Dossier Including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián. items.title: Doktorandin/Doktorand (m/w/d) AG Röder
PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
items.desc: The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI. The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Project description The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team. Description of the scientific environment The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ . This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk ) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk ) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam Who are we looking for? Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems. The PhD programme You can undertake the PhD programme as: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree. Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria: You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; You must work on the project full-time. Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality. Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network Disseminate research nationally and internationally Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project We are looking for the following qualifications: Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position Relevant educational background Relevant publications Relevant work experience Other relevant professional activities Good written and oral English language skills Application and Assessment Procedure Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. Please include : Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications ; Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; Publication list (if available); Names and contact details of three references. Application deadline: The deadline for applications is November 22 , 23:59 GMT +1 . We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements. The further process After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment. The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/. Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December Questions For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position. Vi søger svar og løsninger på fælles problemer og gør ny viden tilgængelig og nyttig for andre. items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology at the University of Oulu (Finland)
items.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are currently looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland. The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) . The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities. The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education. About the job As a doctoral researcher, you will: Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning. Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities . Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers. Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities. Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners. Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results. In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Qualifications To succeed in the position, we expect from you: A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline. A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values. Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research. Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research. Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments. Additional merits considered an advantage Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education . Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers . Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design . Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning . Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments. Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage). What we offer? The support of an experienced and enthusiastic project team of where you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and close-ones in settling into Oulu. We have a HR Excellence in Research -quality label which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, excellent education system, and competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Salary The position is fixed-term for three years as soon as possible or starting from January 2027. The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (maximum of 50% of the job-specific component). Starting gross salary will be approx. 2300-2600 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6 months is applied in the position. How to apply? Interested? If yes, please apply by 15.11.2026 (23:59 Finnish local time) through our recruitment system. The application should be written in English and include the following: Cover letter CV following the guidelines of the Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity Certificates/Diplomas Contact information of two persons available for recommendation The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-site or remote interview. All applicants will be notified during the selection process. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, such as people of different ages, genders and lingual, cultural or minority groups. Contact Information If you have any further questions, please contact D r. items.title: Doctorat (H/F) en Web Sémantique et Intelligence Artificielle
items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Laboratoire d'Informatique, Signaux et Systèmes de Sophia Antipolis Type de Contrat CDD Doctorant Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 06903 VALBONNE Durée du contrat 36 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration 2300,00 € mensuel Date limite de candidature : vendredi 6 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Sujet De Thèse Dans le cadre du projet ANR DIVA, cette thèse se concentrera sur la modélisation sémantique et la représentation en graphes de connaissances de l’activité analytique des utilisateurs, ainsi que sur l’étude d’approches neuro-symboliques pour apprendre et raisonner sur ces représentations. L’objectif est ainsi de poser les fondations nécessaires à la prédiction de comportements et, à terme, au développement de mécanismes de recommandation et d’adaptation des visualisations explicables et contrôlables. Malgré des travaux importants sur la capture et la visualisation des traces d'activité des utilisateurs, les représentations existantes sont généralement propriétaires ou ad hoc [1], ce qui limite le raisonnement automatisé, l'interopérabilité et la réutilisation à long terme. Les graphes de connaissances (GC), fondés sur les normes du Web sémantique telles que RDF, RDFS et OWL, offrent une alternative prometteuse pour représenter l'activité des utilisateurs sous forme de données liées et riches sur le plan sémantique [3]. Ils permettent notamment de structurer et intégrer des données d'activité hétérogènes, tout en fournissant des mécanismes standardisés d'interrogation et de raisonnement. Cette représentation constitue ainsi un support pertinent pour l'application de méthodes d'IA visant à identifier des comportements analytiques et à en prédire l'évolution, tout en conservant une représentation explicite et interprétable des connaissances. S'appuyant sur des travaux antérieurs (par exemple, UI2Ont [4] et DIVA [5], et des ensembles de données ouverts sur l'activité des utilisateurs [6], cette thèse de doctorat vise à développer des modèles sémantiques et des approches neuro-symboliques pour la représentation et l'analyse de l'activité utilisateur. Elle s'articule autour des objectifs suivants : Modélisation sémantique de l'activité de l'utilisateur : Développer un cadre unifié, fondé sur des vocabulaires RDF, pour représenter l'activité multimodale de l'utilisateur sous forme de GC, en intégrant et structurant les données hétérogènes générées lors de l'exploration visuelle, notamment les interactions de l'utilisateur, le suivi du regard et les verbalisations. Découverte et prédiction du comportement exploratoire de l'utilisateur : Étudier des méthodes neuro-symboliques permettant d'exploiter les GC pour découvrir et prédire des comportements exploratoires, en combinant apprentissage automatique et raisonnement symbolique afin d'identifier des modèles comportementaux interprétables. Raffinement dynamique et validation des modèles comportamentaux : Étudier des méthodes de raffinement incrémental des modèles et règles comportementaux au cours de l'exploration, et évaluer leur qualité, leur interprétabilité et leurs capacités prédictives dans différents scénarios d'utilisation. Plan de travail : La thèse débutera par une revue de l’état de l’art, suivie du développement et de la validation du modèle sémantique et des pipelines de construction des graphes de connaissances. Les travaux porteront ensuite sur la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires à l’aide de méthodes neuro-symboliques, puis sur leur raffinement dynamique et incrémental. Les approches développées seront évaluées sur des données réelles et donneront lieu à des publications scientifiques ainsi qu’à des contributions open source. Les livrables attendus sont : L1. Modèle sémantique et extension de DIVA-O pour l’activité utilisateur multimodale. L2. Pipeline de construction et d’enrichissement des graphes de connaissances. L3. Méthodes neuro-symboliques pour la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires. L4. Méthodes de raffinement dynamique des modèles comportementaux. L5. Évaluation expérimentale des modèles et méthodes proposés. L6. Publications scientifiques et ressources open source. Références Bibliographiques [3] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces – Yet Another User Interface Description Language?,” 2011. [4] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “UI2Ont—A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces and Interactions,” in Semantic Models for Adaptive Interactive Systems, T. Hussein, H. Paulheim, S. Lukosch, J. Ziegler, and G. Calvary, Eds., London: Springer, 2013, pp. 1–24. doi: 10.1007/978-1-4471-5301-6_1. [5] A. Menin and C. Faron, “DIVA: An Ontology-based Approach to Model User Activity within Visualization Systems,” in SAC 2026 - 41st ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing, Thessaloniki, Greece, Mar. 2026. doi: 10.1145/3748522.3779893. [6] S. Mohseni, A. Pachuilo, E. H. Nirjhar, R. Linder, A. Pena, and E. D. Ragan, “Analytic Provenance Datasets: A Data Repository of Human Analysis Activity and Interaction Logs,” Jan. 16, 2018, arXiv: arXiv:1801.05076. doi: 10.48550/arXiv.1801.05076. Votre Environnement de Travail Cette thèse est accueillie par le laboratoire I3S du CNRS à l’Université Côte d’Azur. Plus précisément, le/la doctorant(e) rejoindra l’équipe Wimmics (Inria, Université Côte d’Azur, CNRS, I3S), qui mène des recherches à l’interface entre intelligence artificielle et Web, notamment autour des graphes de connaissances, de la représentation et du traitement sémantique des données, et des méthodes d’IA pour les données du Web. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR JCJC DIVA, qui vise à étudier comment l’activité des utilisateurs avec des systèmes de visualisation interactifs peut être capturée, représentée et exploitée afin de mieux comprendre et, à terme, accompagner leurs processus d’analyse. Le projet part du constat que les interactions des utilisateurs avec les visualisations constituent une source riche d’information sur leurs processus analytiques, leurs stratégies et leurs objectifs, mais que les approches existantes reposent souvent sur des représentations ad hoc, limitant leur interopérabilité, leur réutilisation et le raisonnement automatisé [1], [2]. DIVA vise ainsi à développer des approches sémantiques et neuro-symboliques pour représenter l’activité des utilisateurs et identifier des comportements analytiques à partir de leurs traces d’interaction avec le système, des données biometriques, ainsi que des verbalisations sur leur raisonnement. Références [1] K. Xu, A. Ottley, C. Walchshofer, M. Streit, R. Chang, and J. Wenskovitch, “Survey on the Analysis of User Interactions and Visualization Provenance,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 39, no. 3, pp. 757–783, 2020. [2] F. Yanez, C. Conati, A. Ottley, and C. Nobre, “The State of the Art in User‐Adaptive Visualizations,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 44, Dec. 2024, doi: 10.1111/cgf.15271. items.title: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience
items.desc: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience We are looking for a PhD candidate to join the Multimodal Imaging in Clinical Neuroscience department at the Institute of Neuroscience and Medicine – Medical Imaging Physics (INM-4). You will work in the field of translational neuroscience and precision psychiatry under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar. The brain mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders are poorly understood, and treatment choices are largely symptom-based. In this project, you will use multimodal neuroimaging and computational neuroscience to study how brain networks change in these disorders. The aim is to identify imaging biomarkers that could support earlier diagnosis, predict disease trajectories at an individual level and help match treatment to the patient. A key resource is our MINDset platform (Multimodal Imaging Infrastructure for Neuroscience Data Science), which consolidates over 1,000 multimodal datasets from clinical studies, including structural and functional MRI, PET, EEG, fNIRS, neuropsychological and clinical measures, and digital phenotyping. Vertragsart: Vollzeit Angebot Team & Environment: You will work in a motivated and interdisciplinary team including psychiatrists, neuroscientists, physicists, engineers, and data scientists Research & Infrastructure: You will have access to advanced neuroimaging infrastructure and training in structural and functional MRI, multimodal imaging, connectomics, and computational neuroscience Networking & Exchange: You will participate in (international) conferences and project meetings, actively building your scientific network through collaborations involving Forschungszentrum Jülich, RWTH Aachen University, Ulm University, Bezirkskrankenhaus Günzburg and LVR-Klinik Cologne Supervision & Support: We will accompany your doctoral studies with continuous, expert guidance from your academic supervisors Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar Work-life balance: Optimal conditions for balancing work and private life, as well as a family-friendly company policy. The option of flexible working (in terms of location) is generally available after consultation and in line with upcoming tasks and (on-site) appointments Annual Leave: You get 30 days of annual leave Fixed-term: The position is limited to 3 years Fair remuneration: Depending on your existing qualifications and the tasks assigned to you, you will be classified in pay grade 13 (65 %) of the TVöD-Bund (Collective Agreement for the Public Service). In addition to the basic salary, there is an additional year-end bonus under the collective pay agreement amounting to 75% of a monthly salary, as well as capital-forming benefits. All information on the TVöD-Bund collective agreement can be found on the BMI website. The monthly salaries in euros can be found on page 74 of the PDF download Support for international employees: Our International Advisory Service makes it easier for international employees to get started In addition to exciting tasks and a collegial working environment, we offer you much more: https://go.fzj.de/benefits Aufgaben The successful candidate will have the opportunity to combine prospectively acquired data with existing multimodal datasets and contribute to replication studies, biomarker development, machine learning applications, and analyses of individual disease trajectories. Your tasks will include: Integrate multimodal neuroimaging datasets from MRI, PET, EEG, and fNIRS studies Characterize brain networks using graph-theoretical methods and structural and functional connectivity analyses Apply multivariate statistical modelling and machine learning to multimodal datasets Investigate individualized imaging biomarkers relevant to diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring Coordinate longitudinal studies involving psychiatric patients and healthy controls, including recruitment, scheduling, and neuropsychological and psychopathological assessments Coordinate and supervise MRI data acquisition; maintain standardized acquisition protocols and data quality Manage and curate imaging data in accordance with established standards (e.g., BIDS) Profil Excellent university degree (Master) in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, medical physics, psychology, cognitive science, computer science, physics, data science, or a related discipline A strong interest in translational psychiatry, neuroimaging and computational neuroscience, and a motivation to work in an interdisciplinary research environment Programming experience in MATLAB and/or Python, alongside strong analytical and problem-solving skills Experience with structural and/or functional MRI; familiarity with packages such as SPM, FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI, MRtrix, CONN, or similar tools is desirable Knowledge of neuroimaging preprocessing, quality control, graph theory, connectomics, multivariate statistics, or machine learning is an advantage Very good command of written and spoken English with extensive vocabulary is required (at least B2 level according to the CEFR), ideally supported by a certificate confirming the language level German language skills at B1 level are desirable Über uns We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, e.g. in terms of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation / identity, and social, ethnic and religious origin. A diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities in which everyone can realize their potential is important to us. The following links provide further information on diversity and equal opportunities: https://go.fzj.de/equality and on specific support options for women: https://go.fzj.de/womens-job-journey. International applicants can find more information here: https://go.fzj.de/job-journey-internationals

items.desc: Sustainability, in its broadest definition, is the cornerstone of research and education in the Department of Built Environment. We take the lead in (re)shaping the built environment to be future-proof, safe, healthy, inclusive and respectful of planetary boundaries. We house the entire spectrum of technology, engineering, design, and human behavior disciplines in the built environment, with world-class experimental facilities at all scales. This allows us to address societal challenges from a uniquely integrated perspective. Introduction Are you a graduate in exact sciences, engineering or econometrics, passionate about using data and AI to improve people's lives?Eindhoven University of Technology is looking for a PhD candidate to develop innovative data-driven solutions that predict and optimise the impact of housing improvements on children's health and wellbeing. Job Description Millions of children, even in high-income countries, are born and grow up in homes with poor insulation, inadequate heating, or insufficient ventilation, affecting their health and development. While housing upgrades are often motivated by sustainability and affordability goals, we focus on their potential benefits for future generations. How does inadequate housing during pregnancy and early childhood affect children's health and development? Which housing upgrades offer the greatest benefits? And how can behavioural modelling, big data and AI help shape healthier, more equitable homes? These are the questions your PhD research will tackle. You will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers and practitioners, working at the intersection of housing, public health, climate adaptation, and social equity. Combining medical and behavioural insights, large-scale data analysis, computer vision and advanced statistical methods, you will be tranforming complex unstructured housing and health data into predictive models. The results will feed into a digital tool to predict and optimise the impact of housing upgrades across different scenarios, helping housing providers and municipalities create healthier, more resilient homes for families. This research is part of the NWO-funded research programme Homes for Upcoming Generations, which brings together social scientists, medical doctors, building engineers and industry partners. items.title: PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point ultrasound'
items.desc: Jouw functie Ultrasound and tomosynthesis are the most prevalent modalities used for breast imaging, and each has its specific advantages and disadvantages. Ultrasound uses sound waves to create a cross-sectional image of the tissue and has excellent depth resolution, but limited resolution in directions perpendicular to the transmitted ultrasound lines. Tomosynthesis uses x rays to create a pseudo-3D representation of the breast with high in-plane spatial resolution, but low out-of-plane (depth) resolution. Therefore, both techniques are complementary to each other. We plan to develop a joint system that will use the information from each modality to improve the image quality of the other, yielding not only a multi-modality imaging system, but a joint imaging system. The combination of tomosynthesis and ultrasound into a single joint imaging system will yield improved images from two independent and complementary sources, with inherent spatial correlation, allowing for improved lesion detection, even in dense breasts, and the direct multi-modal assessment of suspicious lesions. For this multi-disciplinary project, we will be working in collaboration with the Advanced X-ray Tomography Imaging (AXTI) lab of our Department, who will be developing the X-ray aspects of this system (see accompanying vacancy). In this project, you will focus on 3D ultrasound by using an ultra-wide ultrasound transducer that is mounted in a paddle required for acquisition of tomosynthesis data. In this way, a 3D ultrasound dataset can be acquired that can be used to improve the x-ray data by using the high-axial resolution US data. Additionally, the ultrasound data can be improved by using the high-resolution x-ray data. You will develop and validate these methods using both digital and physical phantoms, working towards first patient images at the end of the project. All of this will be in collaboration with a PhD student focusing on the x-ray aspects of the project, and industry partners to facilitate the translation of these methods into clinical evaluation. Tasks will also include presenting at international scientific conferences and writing papers on the newly developed methods and study results. PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point X-ray' Jouw werkplek Nijmegen and the Radboudumc Nijmegen is the oldest Dutch city with a rich history and one of the liveliest city centers in the Netherlands. Radboud University has over 17,000 students. Radboud University Medical Center is a leading academic center for medical science, education, and health care with over 10,000 staff and 3,000 students. Department of Medical Imaging The Department of Medical Imaging is one of the most active research departments of the Radboudumc. More than 200 researchers are continuously striving to optimize healthcare. Close cooperation between preclinical researchers, radiologists, and clnicians gives a fantastic opportunity to implement new imaging techniques in clinical practice, and you will be working directly in this field. Medical Ultrasound Imaging Center: MUSIC The MUSIC laboratory works on the development, optimization, and clinical evaluation of new ultrasound imaging methods. For that, MUSIC collaborates with major vendors of ultrasound equipment. The focus of MUSIC is on development of high end ultrasound solutions for improved diagnosis of breast cancer, carotid diseases, and liver steatosis. Additionally, AI-driven handheld ultrasound solutions are developed for improving diagnosis in low resource settings, and by general practitioners and doctors in child consultation centers. For this, the group has researchers with various backgrounds, from engineering to medical doctors, providing wide-ranging expertise in image reconstruction and processing, deep learning and other AI methods, and analysis, along with the design and performance of patient trials. The laboratory works closely with radiologists and industry. items.title: PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point X-ray'
items.desc: Jouw functie Ultrasound and tomosynthesis are the most prevalent modalities used for breast imaging, and each has its specific advantages and disadvantages. Tomosynthesis uses x rays to create a pseudo-3D representation of the breast with high in-plane spatial resolution, but low out-of-plane (depth) resolution. Ultrasound uses sound waves to create a cross-sectional image of the tissue and has excellent depth resolution, but limited resolution in directions perpendicular to the transmitted ultrasound lines. We plan to develop a joint system that will use the information from each modality to improve the image quality of the other, yielding not only a multi-modality imaging system, but a joint imaging system. The combination of tomosynthesis and ultrasound into a single joint imaging system will yield improved images from two independent and complementary sources, with inherent spatial correlation, allowing for improved lesion detection, even in dense breasts, and the direct multi-modal assessment of suspicious lesions. For this multi-disciplinary project, we will be working in collaboration with the Medical UltraSound Imaging Center (MUSIC) lab of our Department, who will be developing the ultrasound aspects of this system (see accompanying vacancy). In this project you will focus on the x-ray related data preprocessing and on the joint reconstruction itself. You will validate these using both digital and physical phantoms, working towards first patient images at the end of the project. All of this will be in collaboration with a PhD student focusing on the ultrasound aspects of the project, and industry partners to facilitate the translation of these methods into clinical evaluation. Tasks will also include presenting at international scientific conferences and writing papers on the newly developed methods and study results. PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point ultrasound' Jouw werkplek Nijmegen and the Radboudumc Nijmegen is the oldest Dutch city with a rich history and one of the liveliest city centers in the Netherlands. Radboud University has over 17,000 students. Radboud University Medical Center is a leading academic center for medical science, education, and health care with over 10,000 staff and 3,000 students. Department of Medical Imaging The Department of Medical Imaging is one of the most active research departments of the Radboudumc. More than 100 researchers are continuously striving to optimize healthcare. Close cooperation between preclinical researchers, radiologists, and clinicians gives a fantastic opportunity to implement new imaging techniques in clinical practice, and you will be working directly in this field. Advanced X-ray Tomographic Imaging laboratory The AXTI laboratory works on the development, optimization, and clinical evaluation of new x-ray-based imaging methods. The lab focuses on the use of medical physics approaches to improve image acquisition, reconstruction, and processing methods, including artificial intelligence algorithms, and to evaluate the clinical performance of new technology in new clinical applications. The group counts on members with wide-ranging expertise in image processing, reconstruction, deep learning and other AI methods, and analysis, as well as radiation dosimetry, along with the design and performance of patient trials. The laboratory works closely with radiologists and industry to develop new, clinically relevant, imaging methods and processes in x-ray-based imaging, especially in breast imaging and body CT, to have an impact in detection, diagnosis, and treatment of pathologies. items.title: PhD Autonomous & Decentralized Air Traffic Management
items.desc: Functieomschrijving Background Air Traffic Management (ATM) and Communications, Navigation, and Surveillance (CNS) systems form the operational foundation of civil aviation. Current operations depend heavily on centralized ground facilities and satellite services for surveillance and management. This system is vulnerable for a range of disruptions including infrastructure failures, GNSS outages or cyber incidents. These vulnerabilities can degrade or even halt civil aviation. Project ORION (Onboard Resilient Infrastructure-free Operational Network) investigates an alternative ATM/CNS architecture designed to function without reliance on ground- or space-based infrastructure. By utilizing an aeronautical ad-hoc network for communication, relative positioning, and surveillance, ORION aims to enable aircraft to self-organize and maintain safe separation thus ensuring a minimum service level even during (large scale) disruptions. Project description This PhD project is fundamentally multidisciplinary. As a PhD candidate, you will design, model, and evaluate a decentralized ATM/CNS architecture. The research focuses on determining how core traffic management functions can be sustained through cooperation using an aeronautical network when centralized ground and satellite services are unavailable. In the first phase of the research, you will determine a set of use cases and design the underlying aeronautical ad-hoc networking concept layer to enable direct airborne data exchange, cooperative relative localization, and cooperative surveillance. Next, building on this network layer, you will formulate distributed algorithms for fundamental traffic management functions, including aircraft-as-a-sensor (mesh network), separation assurance, conflict detection and resolution, and traffic sequencing. Finally, to evaluate the operational feasibility of the architecture, you will implement the models within an ATM simulation platform, such as the open-source simulator BlueSky. For this you will extend the platform to include the ad-hoc networking functionality. Using this environment, you will stress-test the system under severe disruption scenarios by comparing the overall performance directly against conventional centralized ATM/CNS operations. This will provide evidence of the performance of the models for the various use-cases. Your profile Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field; Strong analytical and mathematical foundation, with experience in or a keen aptitude for complex systems modelling and distributed systems; Multidisciplinary mindset with the ability to bridge distinct domains: connecting operational ATM concepts with distributed network protocols and algorithm design; Strong background in programming, using Python or other relevant programming languages; Good scientific reporting and communication skills in written and spoken English. What we offer you You will receive a 4-year research contract from NLR and will join the Air Traffic department. In addition, you will be enrolled in the Doctoral Education programme of the Graduate School at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). During this period, you will work closely with NLR colleagues in Amsterdam and with academic supervisors from TU Delft. Your working week will ideally be divided into: 2 days in Amsterdam, 2 days in Delft, and 1 day from home. In addition, we offer: No fewer than 45 days off (with full-time employment); A fixed end-of-year bonus of 8%; A contribution towards your healthcare costs; Extra paid parental leave; The possibility to work from home where possible. Would you like to know more? Please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/en/ae/research/ae-graduate-school for more information on the graduate school. For more information about the recruitment procedure, contact Pien Moller (recruiter) via pien.moller@nlr.nl. Would you like to apply? Great, we are curious about you! Send your motivation letter and CV via the apply button ! A pre-employment security screening (VGB-C) is a requirement. For more information about the screening, please visit the AIVD website. items.title: PhD Position in Bidirectional Power Converter Design and Control for Data Centers
items.desc: The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Introduction Data centers are the backbone of the digital economy, but their exponential growth in energy consumption-driven by AI and machine learning workloads-demands transformative solutions. The next-generation of data centers will be based on Solid-State Transformer, which enables energy distribution with higher efficiency, grid-friendly data center operation and etc. This PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of power electronics, control systems, and grid integration, with direct collaboration with Delta Energy System GmbH, a global leader in power conversion for data centers. Your research will focus on power electronics converters for SST, focusing on the DC-DC stage. Job Description As a PhD candidate in the Electromechanics and Power Electronics (EPE) group at TU/e, you will with solid-state transformers (SST) for datacenter, focusing on the DC-DC stage. Your research will address the critical challenges of power density, efficiency, and grid stability in modern data centers, focusing on the converter design and advanced control/modulation strategies to achieve high performance and high controllability. Additionally, the design should be validate with experimental results. Your work will directly contribute to the sustainability of AI infrastructure by enabling data centers to efficiently integrate renewable energy sources, support grid stability, and reduce their carbon footprint. With access to cutting-edge tools and industrial collaboration, you will have the opportunity to shape the future of power electronics for data centers. Job Requirements A master's degree (or equivalent university degree) in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Control Systems, or a related field. A research-oriented attitude with strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interest in collaborating with industrial partners. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Based on our candidate assessment, the following skills are valuable: Required: Demonstrated knowledge in power converter topologies (e.g., DC-DC, AC-DC, multilevel converters). Familiarity with control theory (e.g., classical control, state-space methods, model predictive control). Experience with simulation tools (MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, or similar). Understanding of grid integration challenges (e.g., power quality, stability, renewable energy interfacing). Advantageous: Hands-on experience with prototyping and experimental validation of power converters. Affinity with embedded systems (DSP, FPGA) for real-time control implementation. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here.
