items.title: 3 PhD Candidates in Material Science and Energy Engineering
items.desc: Career Vacant positions Job vacancy 3 PhD Candidates in Material Science and Energy Engineering SINTEF Industry, Department of Metal Production and Processing (MPP) & Department of Sustainable Energy Technology (BET) and announce three PhD candidate position within the field of Energy engineering and material science. The position is within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidates will be employed by the Casting, Forming, and Recycling and Solar Energy and Materials research groups during the doctoral project, enrolled by the doctoral program at Brunel University of London , and have supervisors both at SINTEF and Brunel, College of Engineering, Design and Physical Science. As part of the MSCA Doctoral Network programme, the successful candidate will undertake a secondment with one of the project's industrial partners. This position’s scope is Integrated Modelling of Thermal Energy Flows, Waste Heat Recovery, and High-Temperature Heat Pump Deployment in Industrial Clusters. Development and Validation of Modular Digital Twin Frameworks for Industrial High-Temperature Heat Pump Integration Developing Decarbonisation Pathways for Industrial Heat Through High-Temperature Heat Pumps, Renewable Energy Integration, and Thermal Storage The activity is coordinated within the MSCA-DN by the Brunel University of London. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 6 partners and 12 Associated partners across Europe. The project aims to undertake cutting-edge multidisciplinary research and development to make a step change in the understanding of Industrial High Temperature Heat Pump (IHTHP) technology, both at the overall system and component levels while addressing sustainability, economic social impact and energy policy aspects to support realising its potential to provide a breakthrough towards full industrial heat decarbonisation helping to achieve the 2050 net-zero emissions targets. The topics hosted by SINTEF is "Mapping Industrial Energy Flows and Developing Decarbonisation Pathways for IHTHP Integration" and focus on developing data-driven strategies for industrial heat decarbonisation by mapping energy flows, integrating HTHPs with low-carbon technologies, and creating decision-support databases for system design and sustainability assessment. "Development of Digital Twin Frameworks for Predictive Modelling and Optimisation of IHTHPs" and focus on developing and validating digital twin frameworks for the integration and optimisation of IHTHPs in high-temperature industrial processes, enhancing the understanding of industrial energy flows and optimisation strategies, and enabling factory-wide digital energy management systems to support industrial digitalisation, energy efficiency, and decarbonisation. "Grid integration and sector coupling challenges of electrifying industrial heat using IHTHPs" and focus integrating IHTHPs, renewable energy, and thermal storage to enhance grid flexibility, support industrial decarbonisation, and enable scalable low-carbon heat solutions. The project combines engineering analysis with industrial implementation perspectives, including decision-support methodologies, stakeholder engagement, business case development, techno-economic assessments, innovation management, and pathways for industrial adoption of low-carbon technologies. SINTEF MPP & BET and HeatMinds partners have extensive expertise in Industrial High Temperature Heat Pumps (IHTHPs), thermal systems engineering, energy systems modelling, thermal heat storage, digital twin, waste heat recovery and utilisation, process metallurgy, industrial decarbonisation, data analytics and digitalisation, and socio-economic analysis. The project includes international secondments at academic and industrial institutions and close collaboration with the related PhD positions at Brunel. Contacts Topic 1 and 3 Morten Ingar Onsøien and Sarina Bao Topic 2 and 3 Gaute Stokkan and Eivind Johannes Øvrelid Work place: SINTEF Trondheim and Nordland (secondment partners). Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondments with HeatMinds partners. Participate in conferences, workshops and training activities. Adjust project focus as the PhD progresses if needed. Complete doctoral education. Participate actively in the Casting, Forming, and Recycling and Solar Energy and Materials two research groups. Required selection criteria Relevant Master's degree in Material Science, Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Process Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Sustainable Energy Systems, Industrial Ecology, Technology Management, Engineering Management, Systems Engineering, Industrial Digitalisation, or similar. Experience with data analytics, decision-support systems, digitalisation, industrial management, innovation management, technology transfer, project portfolio management, or industrial transformation projects is considered an advantage Degree completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential. Excellent written and spoken English. Applicants must meet one of the following English language requirements: IELTS 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in all components), PTE Academic 59 (minimum 59 in all subscores), BrunELT 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in all components), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 (minimum 4.5 in all subscores). Further details on accepted qualifications can be found on Brunel University's English Language Requirements page. MSCA Mobility Rule At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date. Preferred selection criteria Experience with one or more of energy engineering, material science, thermal energy systems, industrial energy systems, process systems engineering, sustainable energy technology, industrial ecology, energy and environmental engineering, industrial decarbonisation, energy Informatics, and mechanical engineering Experience with one or more of energy flow modelling, process integration modelling, techno-economic modelling, energy system modelling. Familiarity with one or more of industrial waste heat, including energy flow mapping, integration of high-temperature heat pumps (HTHPs) with low-carbon technologies, and development of decision-support databases for system design and sustainability assessment. Candidates with experience in technology management, industrial transformation, digitalisation, data analytics, or technology commercialisation are encouraged to apply. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in international interdisciplinary teams. To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. We offer Exciting research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network. Dynamic, creative and inclusive work environment. Access to cutting-edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. The employment period is 3 years, conditioned on external funding through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services for both SINTEF and Brunel; Eksportkontroll – DEKSA . Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria, will not be able to be employed. The application must include: Motivation letter (max. 1 page) CV Copies of diplomas and transcripts (Bachelor’s and Master’s) Bachelor’s and Master’s diplomas/transcripts Master’s thesis or draft (if recently submitted) Names and contact information of two references Applications without required documentation will not be considered. Documents must be in English. Applicants are requested to indicate in their application which of the three proposed SINTEF PhD research topics they wish to pursue. Unit SINTEF Industry Work place Trondheim Application due 15/11/2026 Questions regarding the position Eivind Johannes Øvrelid Senior Research Scientist Morten Ingar Onsøien Research Manager Gaute Stokkan Research Manager Sarina Bao Senior Research Scientist SINTEF Industri er ett av fem institutt som utgjør SINTEF. Med over 620 medarbeidere, er vi det største instituttet. Vi legger grunnlaget for fremtidens bærekraftige industri. Med vår flerfaglige kunnskapsbase og avanserte laboratorier som fundament, utvikler vi - i tett samarbeid med våre kunder og samarbeidspartnere - teknologi og tverrfaglige løsninger med stor påvirkning på samfunnet innen et bredt spekter av markeds- og fagområder, for eksempel: Sirkulær økonomi, batterier, hydrogen, CCS, materialvitenskap og -teknologi, nanoteknologi, nanomedisin, sol, vind, bioteknologi, metallproduksjon, prosessteknologi, lavutslippsproduksjon av olje og gass og industriell økonomi og optimering. About SINTEF SINTEF is one of Europe’s largest research institutes, offering specialist multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of technology and the natural and social sciences. SINTEF is an independent foundation that since 1950 has generated innovation by means of research and development projects for the private and public sectors both in Norway and overseas. SINTEF has 2,100 employees from 80 countries and an annual turnover of more than NOK three billion. SINTEF invests any profits into further research and innovation. Our vision: Technology for a better society.

items.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. PhD Position in Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Cultures – Securitisation of Religion in Hybrid Regimes: Insights from Central Asia and North Africa Project description This doctoral project investigates how governments in Uzbekistan and Egypt mobilise religious narratives to justify security policies and governance strategies. The doctoral candidate will analyse how religion becomes embedded within state security frameworks and assess the implications of these processes for citizenship, constitutional legitimacy, and state-society relations in hybrid political regimes. To read more about the MINARET project please see: https://www.norca.lu.se/minaret https://www.soclaw.lu.se/en/article/major-eu-grant-lund-led-phd-programme-islamic-legal-cultures Tasks and responsibilities As a doctoral student, you will be admitted to doctoral studies in sociology of law and employed at Lund University. You will: Conduct independent research within the scope of the project. Undertake multi-sited fieldwork in Central Asia and North Africa (Uzbekistan and Egypt) and two mandatory secondments (one academic, one non-academic) abroad. Participate in training events, workshops, and conferences organized by the MINARET Doctoral Network. Collaborate with international supervisors and peers. Contribute to departmental activities, including teaching and seminars (up to 20% of working hours). If selected for the position, you will join NORCA – Nordic Central Asian Studies (www.norca.lu.se) research environment at the Sociology of Law Department, led by Rustamjon Urinboyev who will also serve as your principal supervisor. You will be given sufficient time, guidance, and resources to develop your individual research project, aligned with the overall MINARET project's aims. Doctoral Programme in Sociology of Law The doctoral programme in sociology of law comprises 240 credits (equivalent to four years of full-time study) and concludes with a public defence of the doctoral thesis. You will primarily engage in doctoral studies and work on your dissertation within the field of sociology of law. You will also actively participate in the department’s research environment. In addition to research, the position may include teaching and administrative duties, up to a maximum of 20% of the working time. The working language is primarily English, but you are expected to acquire basic knowledge of Swedish during the employment period. More information about the doctoral programme is available at: https://www.soclaw.lu.se/en/research/doctoral-studies/phd-handbook General Requirements The requirements for admission to third cycle courses and study programs (in accordance with HF, Chapter 7, Section 35) are that the applicant; meets the general and specific entry requirements that the higher education institution may have laid down, and is considered in other respects to have the ability required to benefit from the course or study program. A person meets the general entry requirements for third cycle courses and study programmes if he or she: has been awarded a second cycle qualification prior to the employment decision, has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. Specific Requirements A completed degree at the advanced level in Sociology of Law or another subject deemed relevant by the employer. Doctoral candidates cannot have been awarded a doctoral degree and/or completed more than four years of full-time equivalent research experience. In line with the eligibility criteria and on Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme, doctoral candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (i.e. work, studies) in the hosting country for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. For further information on eligibility criteria and on Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks in general, please refer to: Doctoral Networks - Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions. A minimum of 240 credits, of which at least 60 must be at the advanced level. At least 30 credits in Sociology of Law or a related subject at the advanced level, including a thesis of at least 15 credits. Excellent ability to express yourself in spoken and written English. Strong motivation and ability to work independently under pressure. Good collaboration and communication skills. Merits Knowledge of legal sociology, Islamic legal culture, security studies and hybrid and authoritarian governance literature. Experience with qualitative research methods and fieldwork. Self-motivated, perseverant, and strong writing skills. Collaborative and independent working style. Knowledge of the legal and political contexts of Central Asia, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is considered an asset. What we offer A full-time, fixed-term employment for four years. Competitive employment package. Joint supervision and intersectoral placements. Comprehensive training in research methods, ethics, Open Science, and transferable skills. Assessment Criteria Regulations for employment as a doctoral student can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance. Only those admitted to third-cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral position. In the recruitment process, primary consideration will be given to the applicant’s ability to benefit from the doctoral programme. The research plan, as well as previous theses and published material in Sociology of Law or related subjects within social sciences or law, are important documents for assessing this ability. In addition to pursuing their own doctoral studies, the incumbent may be required to perform duties related to education, research, and administration in accordance with specific provisions in the Higher Education Ordinance. Excellent ability to express oneself in speech and writing is of great importance. As doctoral studies in Sociology of Law are highly demanding, the candidate must be strongly motivated and able to work independently under pressure. Good collaboration and communication skills are also required, as well as strong proficiency in English, both spoken and written. Application The application must include: A cover letter in English (max 1,000 words), including a brief presentation of yourself and your qualifications, as well as a short description of why you are interested in the doctoral programme in Sociology of Law at the Sociology of Law Department, Lund University. A thesis corresponding to at least 15 credits at the advanced level in Sociology of Law or a subject deemed equivalent/relevant, and other relevant publications. If the thesis is written in a language other than Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, or English, a summary of max 1,000 words must be included, outlining the methodology, theory, results/analysis. A CV in English demonstrating eligibility for doctoral studies in Sociology of Law. Degree certificates and transcripts in English. A research proposal of no more than 13,000 characters (including spaces and references), written in English. Please ensure that your proposed research aligns closely with the focus of the PhD project, Securitisation of Religion in Hybrid Regimes: Insights from Central Asia and North Africa . General guidelines for preparing a research plan can be found here: https://www.soclaw.lu.se/en/sites/soclaw.lu.se.en/files/ras_phd_research_plan.pdf Names and contact details of two referees. A writing sample (e.g., master’s thesis or published paper) that demonstrates the applicant’s research and writing skills. Any other documents the applicant wishes to submit in support of the application. Applicants will be assessed based on the above criteria, and top-ranked candidates will be invited for an interview. Gender equality must always be considered. In cases of equal qualifications, the underrepresented gender within the subject at Lund University shall be prioritized, unless valid reasons suggest otherwise. Employment Type The position is full-time (100%) for four years, starting in September 2027. You are required to work on-site in Lund, Sweden. Employment is governed by the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5. Additional Information For questions regarding the MINARET Doctoral Networks Programme and PhD project, please contact Dr. Rustamjon Urinboyev at rustamjon.urinboyev@soclaw.lu.se, Principal Investigator of the MINARET Doctoral Networks programme. For questions about the doctoral programme in sociology of law, please contact Ida Nafstad at ida.nafstad@soclaw.lu.se. For questions about the recruitment process, please contact Ellen Karlsson at ellen.karlsson@sam.lu.se. The Faculty of Social Sciences at Lund University is one of the leading education and research institutions in Sweden and operates both in Lund and Helsingborg. Sociology of law at Lund University is a subject within Social sciences focusing on the relationship between law and society, such as the tension between the formal legislation of the government and the informal emergence of norms in civil society, among other contexts. Research is conducted in fields such as gender and discrimination, AI and machine learning, children's rights, welfare, legal cultures, corruption, migration, financial security and crime. The department offers courses at all levels. The department also runs the bachelor's program in criminology in collaboration with the Department of Sociology. The Sociology of Law Department is keen to engage in cross-disciplinary collaboration and has good contacts with professionals and public authorities. We kindly decline all sales and marketing contacts. A person meets the general entry requirements for third cycle courses and study programmes if he or she: has been awarded a second cycle qualification prior to the employment decision, has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. Specific Requirements A completed degree at the advanced level in Sociology of Law or another subject deemed relevant by the employer. Doctoral candidates cannot have been awarded a doctoral degree and/or completed more than four years of full-time equivalent research experience. In line with the eligibility criteria and on Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme, doctoral candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (i.e. work, studies) in the hosting country for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. For further information on eligibility criteria and on Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks in general, please refer to: Doctoral Networks - Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions. A minimum of 240 credits, of which at least 60 must be at the advanced level. At least 30 credits in Sociology of Law or a related subject at the advanced level, including a thesis of at least 15 credits. Excellent ability to express yourself in spoken and written English. Strong motivation and ability to work independently under pressure. Good collaboration and communication skills. Merits Knowledge of legal sociology, Islamic legal culture, Islamic public administration, comparative constitutional law and hybrid and authoritarian governance literature. Experience with qualitative research methods and fieldwork. Self-motivated, perseverant, and strong writing skills. Collaborative and independent working style. Knowledge of the legal and political contexts of Central Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is considered an asset. What we offer A full-time, fixed-term employment for four years. Competitive employment package. Joint supervision and intersectoral placements. Comprehensive training in research methods, ethics, Open Science, and transferable skills. Assessment Criteria Regulations for employment as a doctoral student can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance. Only those admitted to third-cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral position. In the recruitment process, primary consideration will be given to the applicant’s ability to benefit from the doctoral programme. The research plan, as well as previous theses and published material in Sociology of Law or related subjects within social sciences or law, are important documents for assessing this ability. In addition to pursuing their own doctoral studies, the incumbent may be required to perform duties related to education, research, and administration in accordance with specific provisions in the Higher Education Ordinance. Excellent ability to express oneself in speech and writing is of great importance. As doctoral studies in Sociology of Law are highly demanding, the candidate must be strongly motivated and able to work independently under pressure. Good collaboration and communication skills are also required, as well as strong proficiency in English, both spoken and written. Application The application must include: A cover letter in English (max 1,000 words), including a brief presentation of yourself and your qualifications, as well as a short description of why you are interested in the doctoral programme in Sociology of Law at the Sociology of Law Department, Lund University. A thesis corresponding to at least 15 credits at the advanced level in Sociology of Law or a subject deemed equivalent/relevant, and other relevant publications. If the thesis is written in a language other than Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, or English, a summary of max 1,000 words must be included, outlining the methodology, theory, results/analysis. A CV in English demonstrating eligibility for doctoral studies in Sociology of Law. Degree certificates and transcripts in English. A research proposal of no more than 13,000 characters (including spaces and references), written in English. Please ensure that your proposed research aligns closely with the focus of the PhD project, Civil Islam and Non-Coercive Governance Across Post-Imperial Islamic Societies in Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and North Africa. items.title: PhD in Machine Learning in Medicine
items.desc: About us You will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Lisa Koch, head of the Machine Learning in Medicine Lab (www.mlm-lab.ch). Our research group develops trustworthy machine learning towards clinical use. Our methodological interests include uncertainty quantification, robustness and reliability, representation learning, probabilistic modelling, and causal machine learning, with applications in biomedical imaging, wearable and tabular data. We publish at leading machine learning and medical imaging venues, collaborate closely with clinicians at Inselspital, Bern University Hospital, and maintain close links to research groups across Switzerland and internationally. We are a small and collaborative team and value regular interactions. Bern offers a strong and growing medical AI community and an excellent quality of life. About the project Chronic diseases often develop gradually over years, and their trajectories vary widely between individuals. Understanding this progression is key to early detection and timely intervention. Large multimodal health datasets combining medical imaging, wearable sensor data and clinical measurements now make it possible to study disease progression from multiple perspectives. The goal of this project is to develop machine learning methods that learn from multimodal health data to characterise and model disease progression. Methodological focus areas the candidate may explore include: Multimodal representation learning across imaging, time series and tabular data Disease progression modelling from cross-sectional and sparse longitudinal data Causal machine learning to disentangle disease progression from treatment effects Learning with missing modalities and irregularly sampled signals Fairness and bias in multimodal models across demographic subgroups The candidate We are looking for a curious and motivated PhD candidate with a keen interest in doing machine learning research in the healthcare space. You should hold a Master's degree in a quantitative discipline such as computer science, machine learning, statistics, biomedical or electrical engineering, or similar. You have solid knowledge of the foundations of machine learning, are willing to dig deep to understand a problem, and have strong analytical skills. You have practical experience implementing and evaluating machine learning models in Python. Experience processing biomedical data (imaging, wearable, tabular) is a plus. Application and Contact Applications received by 30 November 2026 will receive full consideration. After the deadline, we may continue to review applications until the position is filled. Applications should include your CV, full transcripts (BSc and MSc), and a cover letter (max 1 page) telling us about your motivation and something you are particularly proud of or passionate about. Questions about the position? For subject-specific questions and information about the position, please contact lisa.koch@unibe.ch Questions about the application? research.udem@insel.ch

items.title: BHF 4-Year PhD Studentships in Cardiovascular Research (Prevention)
items.desc: University of Cambridge, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College London and University of Oxford. Applications are invited for 10 funded 4-year PhD studentships starting in October 2027, as part of the British Heart Foundation (BHF) doctoral training programme focused on preventing cardiovascular disease through innovative, data-driven approaches. This interdisciplinary PhD programme brings together leading researchers from the University of Cambridge, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College London, and the University of Oxford. Students will be trained to work at the intersection of population health, systems biology, and data science/AI, combining expertise across these fields to tackle one of the most pressing challenges in global health. By harnessing large-scale multimodal data and emerging technologies, students will develop new approaches to understand, predict, and prevent heart and circulatory diseases. Students will be based in one of the following institutes: Cambridge (5 studentships), Edinburgh (2 studentships), Imperial (1 Studentship) or Oxford (2 studentships) while benefiting from training, co-supervision, and collaboration across the partner institutions. Projects will span a range of topics including health data science, AI and machine learning, multi-omics, epidemiology, and translational cardiovascular research. Students will be part of a cohort-based programme, gaining access to shared training activities, collaborative networks, and state-of-the-art data resources across the multi-institute partnership. This four-year PhD programme combines interdisciplinary training with in-depth research. In year 1, students will undertake training courses and research rotations (at their host institution) before selecting their PhD project and supervisory team. In years 2-4, students will carry out their PhD research with interdisciplinary supervision. Additional opportunities will include advanced training courses, programme-wide workshops and symposia, and optional placements with our academic or industry partners, including EMBL-European Bioinformatics Institute, Wellcome Sanger Institute, AstraZeneca, Novo Nordisk, Genomics Ltd, Owlstone Medical, ThermoFischer Scientific and Flagship Pioneering. The co-leads of the programme are: Cambridge - Professor Angela Wood Edinburgh - Professor Nicholas Mills Imperial - Associate Professor Michela Noseda Oxford - Professor Sarah Lewington Eligibility Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a first or upper second-class undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline such as statistics, mathematics, computer science, data science, engineering, bioinformatics, epidemiology, biomedical sciences, genetics, public health, or another quantitative or biomedical field, and may also hold a Master's degree in a related subject. Applicants should also demonstrate strong analytical skills, experience working with data or computational methods, and an interest in interdisciplinary research. Strong communication and teamwork skills are essential, and international applicants may need to provide evidence of English language proficiency. Funding The studentship provides: University tuition fees (UK home rate only) A tax-free stipend at the BHF rate Research training and support We invite applications from students who meet the UK residency requirements (home fees). International students who confirm that additional costs of all overseas tuition fees will be covered through other scholarships or funding schemes will also be considered. How to apply Please do not use the University application portals. To apply, please email bhfphdadmin@medschl.cam.ac.uk with the following documents. Curriculum vitae (CV) Two letters of recommendation from your referees, signed Transcripts A cover letter (maximum 2500 characters) outlining your suitability for the PhD programme and indicating your preferred host institutions in order of preference. Please list only institutions that you would be willing to attend if offered a place, even if they are not your first choice. Evidence of competence in English - If required - please see our Competence in English guidance for more information. AI must not be used when writing personal statements and CVs. This prohibition covers the use of AI to help your use of English. Using AI in your application ' Postgraduate Study Application deadline: 8th December 2026 Please quote reference RH51427 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

items.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
items.desc: Tecnun - Escuela de Ingeniería-Universidad de Navarra Tecnun-Escuela de Ingeniería , perteneciente a la Universidad de Navarra , se propone contribuir a la formación profesional, científica y humana de los futuros ingenieros. Desde su creación, en la primavera de 1961, mantiene un equilibrio entre la docencia, la investigación y el servicio a la sociedad, haciendo que estas actividades se complementen entre sí. Actualmente dispone de dos campus : la sede más antigua, ubicada en el campus universitario del Bº de Ibaeta, está integrada por los edificios de laboratorios, el edificio docente y de representación concluido en 1989, y un edificio multiuso, levantado en 1996. La otra sede se encuentra en el Parque Tecnológico de Miramón e integra las aulas y laboratorios de investigación de las áreas de Electricidad, Electrónica y Comunicaciones. Descripción de la oferta Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants Should Submit a Dossier Including Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián.

items.title: R&D Engineer (PhD Student)
items.desc: At ABB , we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world. This position reports to: Technology Manager __ Your Role And Responsibilities We are now looking for an R&D Engineer to join our team at High Power Motors & Generators division in Helsinki, Finland. In this role, you will work as a PhD student for a predefined project and as a part of our Research & Development (R&D) team. As a PhD student, you will pursue your doctoral thesis at Aalto University’s Department of Electrical Engineering and Automation, the Research Group of Electromechanics. This is an excellent opportunity for a freshly graduated M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering to complete their PhD funded by industry. In this R&D Engineer role, you will have the opportunity to contribute to ABB’s success with technology, software, product, and system development. Each day, you will identify and implement innovative solutions to relevant problems. This is a fixed-term role until spring 2030. The role requires physical presence in Helsinki, Finland. The position is within a project focused on integrating recyclability into the design of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) rotors through multi-material topology optimization. The research addresses the reduction of heavy rare-earth elements in NdFeB magnets, and the development of magnet encapsulation methods for safe disassembly and reuse. The project also includes prototyping, experimental validation, and a comprehensive life-cycle assessment (LCA) and life-cycle cost analysis (LCC). You will be mainly accountable for: Working as an independent and reliable contributor in your PhD project with supervision Performing various tasks in the assigned project (e.g., electrical machines, software), from building concepts, gathering requirements to designing, implementing, integrating, testing Publishing research results in high-impact journals and completing doctoral coursework as required by Aalto University Our team dynamics You will join our Design and Method Development team, where you will be able to advance your project with the support of your supervisor and the whole team. Qualifications For The Role In order to be selected, you must be qualified for doctoral studies at Aalto University (more information available at Aalto’s website: Aalto Doctoral Programme in Electrical Engineering) Completion of your Master of Science of Electrical Engineer with grades qualifying for doctoral studies You have a solid background in electromagnetic design and analysis of rotating machines, especially PMSMs You are familiar with numerical methods for finite element simulations You are interested in programming and have good knowledge of a relevant programming language (Python, MATLAB, or equivalent) You are highly motivated to pursue doctoral research in electrical machines at ABB and at Aalto University You are at ease communicating in English at an advanced academic level Familiarity with topology optimization or structural optimization methods is an advantage You hold current VISA/work permit to work in Finland/EU What's in it for you? A funded fixed term doctoral position with ABB employment, while receiving support and contacts from both the industry and university. Benefits Our culture and benefits reflect our values: courage, care, curiosity and collaboration. The most appreciated benefits according to our personnel are at the moment, e.g. an annual performance bonus, employee share acquisition program, continuous learning opportunities, and other wellbeing and family benefits. More About Us The Large Motors and Generators Division offers a comprehensive product portfolio of large AC motors and generators. The Division’s induction, synchronous and special design motors and synchronous generators power critical applications across industry, infrastructure and marine transportation. Combining the best available materials with superior technology, the large motors and generators are designed to operate efficiently and reliably, even for challenging processes or applications and to have low life cycle costs. If you have questions, please contact Technology Manager Jan Westerlund, tel. +358 50 3323795. Apply for the position by October 18th, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application. Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences. Ready to make an impact? Apply today or visit https://www.abb.com to learn more about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

items.title: PhD: 3D-Aware Multi-Object Tracking
items.desc: At IDEMIA, we aim to offer our employees, a dynamic and exciting environment where you have opportunities for career growth and professional development. Internal mobility is a great way for you to energize your career and to build your personal brand. It’s also a great way to explore other functions, professions or countries as IDEMIA operates in different businesses and in 50+ locations around the world. Purpose IDEMIA and Télécom Paris are opening a CIFRE PhD position to address a key challenge in modern multi-object tracking (MOT): how can we design more robust tracking systems in the presence of severe and prolonged occlusions? While current tracking methods have achieved impressive performance, occlusion remains one of the main sources of identity switches, missed detections, and fragmented trajectories, particularly in crowded and unconstrained environments. We are seeking to develop an improved tracking system by exploring the hypothesis that 3D-aware and amodal representations can provide the missing information required to maintain object identity through occlusion. The PhD will investigate how reasoning about the full, potentially occluded extent of an object (amodal tracking) and/or its position and structure in 3D space (3D-aware tracking) can be integrated into a tracking architecture. Particular attention will be given to challenging real-world scenarios involving dense crowds, frequent occlusions, and complex interactions. While the initial focus will be on single-camera tracking, the development of multi-camera tracking systems is of interest, with the objective of exploiting complementary viewpoints and cross-camera geometric consistency to improve identity preservation. The resulting technologies could support IDEMIA's broader biometric and video-security applications, including public-space surveillance, critical infrastructure protection, smart cities, border control, and access management. Key Missions Investigates and develops robust, efficient, and real-time multi-object tracking (MOT) algorithms, with a focus on end-to-end MOT architectures such as MOTIP2 and pedestrian tracking in challenging occlusion scenarios. Explores amodal and 3D-aware representations to enhance tracking performance while addressing the computational and resource constraints of edge devices. Designs experimental methodologies and benchmarks to evaluate proposed approaches against state-of-the-art MOT methods and real-world datasets. Contributes to the design, implementation, and validation of prototypes, with an initial focus on monocular tracking and future extensions toward multi-camera tracking. Keeps up to date with advances in computer vision, multi-object tracking, amodal perception, and 3D scene understanding, identifying and transferring relevant innovations to industrial applications. Communicates research findings to the IDEMIA and Télécom Paris research and engineering communities, contributing to scientific publications and papers submitted to leading computer vision and machine learning venues. Profile & Other Information Solid foundations in deep learning, particularly transformer architectures (attention mechanisms, DETR-style query-based models). Experience with computer vision tasks: object detection, tracking, and/or 3D/geometric vision (depth estimation, neural scene representations). Proficiency in Python and PyTorch. Familiarity with vision-language / foundation models (CLIP-like contrastive models, open-vocabulary detectors) is a plus. Seize all the opportunities of our fast-paced environment. Expect the unexpected.

items.desc: Als Deutsche Zentrale Fachbibliothek für Technik und Naturwissenschaften sichern wir mit unseren zukunftsweisenden Dienstleistungen die infrastrukturellen Voraussetzungen einer qualitativ hochwertigen Informations- und Literaturversorgung für Forschung in Wissenschaft und Industrie. Mit dem Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) arbeiten wir daran, den Austausch und die Nutzung wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse im digitalen Zeitalter zu revolutionieren. Die Technische Informationsbibliothek (TIB), Programmbereich D, Open Research Knowledge Graph, sucht für die Forschungsgruppe Data Science & Digital Libraries (Prof. Dr. Sören Auer) zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:n Wissenschaftliche:n Mitarbeiter:in / Doktorand:in für Natural Language Processing (NLP) und kausale KI (m/w/d) Die Stelle ist für die Dauer der Projektlaufzeit von drei Jahren befristet. Die Einstellung erfolgt vorbehaltlich der finalen Bewilligung der Mittel durch den Drittmittelgeber Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Die regelmäßige Wochenarbeitszeit beträgt 39,80 Stunden (Vollzeit). Der Arbeitsplatz ist grundsätzlich für Teilzeitbeschäftigung geeignet. Mobiles Arbeiten ist unter Berücksichtigung dienstlicher Erfordernisse in begrenztem Umfang möglich. Die Eingruppierung erfolgt in die Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. Ihre Aufgaben Die Stelle ist Teil des Projekts EcoAIRE - AI-assisted hypothesis assessment in invasion biology and the restoration of freshwater ecosystems under fragmented and heterogeneous ecological evidence im Förderprogramm Leibniz-Kooperative Exzellenz. Das Projekt verbindet die Expertise der TIB in der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache und der wissenschaftlichen Wissensrepräsentation mit der ökologischen Expertise des Leibniz-Instituts für Gewässerökologie und Binnenfischerei (IGB) sowie der Expertise des Deutschen Forschungszentrums für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) in der kausalen Modellierung. An der TIB liegt Ihr Forschungsschwerpunkt auf der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache zur Extraktion wissenschaftlicher und kausaler Informationen. Sie entwickeln Methoden, die wissenschaftliche Evidenz in strukturierte, maschinenverarbeitbare Repräsentationen von Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Unsicherheiten und kausalen Zusammenhängen überführen. Dabei geht Ihre Forschung über die Extraktion einzelner Fakten hinaus: Sie modellieren, wie wissenschaftliche Befunde zusammenhängen und unter welchen Bedingungen wissenschaftliche Aussagen gelten. Darauf aufbauend erforschen Sie kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern. Dazu gehören Simulationen, interventionsbasierte Schlussfolgerungsverfahren und die Bewertung von Hypothesen unter veränderten Bedingungen. Ihre Tätigkeit umfasst Sie entwickeln ein multimodales Rahmenwerk, das heterogene wissenschaftliche Wissensquellen - darunter Publikationen, Bilder, ergänzende Informationen, Datensätze und weitere Forschungsartefakte - in strukturierte Repräsentationen zur Hypothesenbewertung integriert und dabei die Herkunft der Informationen nachvollziehbar berücksichtigt. Sie entwickeln sprachmodellbasierte und agentenbasierte Methoden, um Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Evidenz, Unsicherheiten sowie kausale oder mechanistische Zusammenhänge quellenübergreifend zu extrahieren, zu vereinheitlichen, aufeinander abzustimmen und zusammenzuführen. Sie erforschen kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern, um Interventionen zu simulieren und zu untersuchen, inwieweit sich Hypothesen auf veränderte Bedingungen übertragen lassen. Sie entwickeln Evaluationsrahmenwerke, die unterschiedliche Qualitätsaspekte der KI-gestützten Hypothesenbewertung erfassen. Dazu gehören Verfahren auf Grundlage fachlicher Expertenbewertungen sowie Ansätze, bei denen große Sprachmodelle als Bewertungsinstanz eingesetzt werden („LLM-as-a-judge“). Sie veröffentlichen Ihre Forschungsergebnisse auf Konferenzen und in Fachzeitschriften mit Peer-Review-Verfahren in den Bereichen NLP, Semantic Web, künstliche Intelligenz und maschinelles Lernen. Zudem wirken Sie an Projektberichten und der Verbreitung der Forschungsergebnisse mit. Ihr Profil Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master oder gleichwertiger Abschluss) in Informatik oder einem eng verwandten Fachgebiet, beispielsweise Künstliche Intelligenz (Artificial Intelligence), maschinelle Sprachverarbeitung (Natural Language Processing), maschinelles Lernen (Machine Learning), Data Science oder Computerlinguistik. Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Forschung oder Softwareentwicklung mit Python sowie praktische Kenntnisse moderner Methoden der Softwareentwicklung, beispielsweise Git-basierter Zusammenarbeit, automatisierter Tests und reproduzierbarer Experimente. Nachweisbare praktische Erfahrung mit transformerbasierten Modellen und großen Sprachmodellen, einschließlich der Nutzung von Frameworks wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers oder vergleichbaren Technologien für NLP-Anwendungen. Praktische Erfahrung in der Entwicklung agentenbasierter KI-Workflows oder von Multiagenten-KI-Workflows, einschließlich Werkzeugnutzung, strukturierter Ausgaben, Orchestrierung oder iterativer Verarbeitungspipelines für Schlussfolgerungen. Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens dem Niveau C1 für die wissenschaftliche Kommunikation, Zusammenarbeit und Publikationstätigkeit. Wünschenswerte Qualifikationen Erfahrung mit der Feinabstimmung oder Anpassung großer Sprachmodelle und/oder dem Aufbau fortgeschrittener RAG-Pipelines unter Verwendung von Technologien wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Sentence Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex, FAISS, Qdrant oder vergleichbaren Werkzeugen. Dazu zählen embeddingbasierte Informationssuche, Reranking, Vektorsuche und strukturierte Generierung. Kenntnisse der kausalen Modellierung und kausalen Inferenz, beispielsweise kausaler Graphen, struktureller Kausalmodelle oder interventionsbasierter Schlussfolgerungsverfahren. Erfahrung mit Semantic-Web-Technologien. Fachkenntnisse in der Ökologie, insbesondere der Süßwasserökologie, Invasionsbiologie oder Renaturierungsökologie, oder Erfahrung in der Mitarbeit an interdisziplinären wissenschaftlichen Projekten. Wir bieten Unser Ziel ist es, die Bereitstellung und Nutzung von Forschungsdaten und -informationen immer wieder neu zu überdenken und zu innovieren. Wir bieten ein intellektuell inspirierendes Umfeld mit unternehmerischer Denkweise, eingebettet in eine führende technische Universität und eines der größten Informationszentren der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Mit dem Forschungszentrum L3S der Leibniz Universität Hannover, eines der weltweit führenden Forschungsinstitute im Bereich Web & Data Science, besteht dabei im Rahmen des Leibniz Joint Lab Data Science & Open Knowledge eine enge Kooperation. Nicht zuletzt legen wir Wert auf ein offenes und kreatives Arbeitsklima, in dem es Spaß macht zu arbeiten. Darüber hinaus bieten wir einen gemeinwohlorientierten Arbeitsplatz im öffentlichen Dienst auf der Grundlage des TV-L mit einer Vergütung nach der Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. eine Sonderzahlung zum Jahresende sowie 30 Tage Urlaub im Jahr bei einer Fünf-Tage-Woche sowie zusätzliche freie Tage an Heiligabend (24.12.) und Silvester (31.12.). einen flexiblen Arbeitsplatz in Zeit und Raum mit Angeboten zur Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie wie u. a. mobiles Arbeiten und flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodellen (Gleitzeit). einen modernen Arbeitsplatz in zentraler Lage von Hannover mit einem kollegialen, attraktiven und vielseitigen Arbeitsumfeld. einen Arbeitgeber mit breit gefächertem Fort- und Weiterbildungsangebot, einer betrieblichen Gesundheitsförderung und Altersvorsorge für den öffentlichen Dienst (VBL). Beschäftigtenrabatt in den Mensen des Studentenwerks Hannover sowie vergünstigte Möglichkeit zur Nutzung der vielseitigen Angebote des Hochschulsports Hannover. eigenverantwortliche und zukunftsorientierte Tätigkeiten, die Abwechslung bieten und Raum für persönliche Entwicklung lassen. die Finanzierung der erforderlichen Ausstattung sowie von Reisen zu Konferenzen und Forschungsaufenthalten. die Mitarbeit in einem nationalen Forschungs- und Innovationsprojekt. ein breites Spektrum an Forschungsinfrastrukturen und Technologiekomponenten, auf denen Sie aufbauen können. Dazu gehören TIB AIssistant, der Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG), ORKG Ask sowie Forschungssoftware aus dem SciKnowOrg-Ökosystem. Interessent:innen können sich bei Frau Dr. Jennifer D’Souza, Leitung der Organisationseinheit „NLP for Scientific Information“ innerhalb der Forschungsgruppe Data Science and Digital Libraries, per E-Mail unter Jennifer.dsouza@tib.eu näher über das Arbeitsgebiet informieren. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung bis zum 14.11.2026 . Um Ihre Bewerbung einzureichen, klicken Sie bitte hier. Bewerbungen in Papierform sind ebenfalls gleichrangig möglich. Für diesen Fall senden Sie Ihre vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen bitte unter Angabe der Ausschreibungsnummer 44/2026 bis zum 14.11.2026 an die Technische Informationsbibliothek (TIB) Personalservice Herrn Daniel Ridder Welfengarten 1 B 30167 Hannover oder als PDF-Datei an Bewerbung@tib.eu. Bei einer Bewerbung in digitalisierter Form bitten wir um Übersendung einer einzigen PDF-Datei mit einer Größe von maximal 10 MB. Wir laden Sie ein, Ihrer Bewerbung eine Angabe Ihrer jährlichen Gehaltsvorstellung beizufügen. Bei ausländischen Hochschulabschlüssen ist zur abschließenden Beurteilung der Einstellungsvoraussetzungen im Laufe des Einstellungsverfahrens zwingend eine Zeugnisbewertung der Zentralstelle für Ausländisches Bildungswesen (ZAB) vorzulegen (Link für mehr Informationen). Hierbei fallen Gebühren an. Diese Pflicht entfällt, sofern der ausländische Hochschulabschluss bereits gutachterlich beurteilt worden ist und in der ANABIN-Datenbank der ZAB als gleichwertiger Hochschulabschluss aufgeführt wird (Link zur ANABIN-Datenbank). Wer wir sind Die TIB ist eine Stiftung öffentlichen Rechts des Landes Niedersachsen. Mit rund 600 Beschäftigten und einem Etat von circa 60 Millionen Euro ist sie eine der größten Informationsinfrastruktureinrichtungen in Deutschland. Die TIB sorgt für optimale Arbeitsbedingungen und baut Maßnahmen zur Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie kontinuierlich aus. Sie will die Gleichberechtigung von Frauen und Männern besonders fördern und fordert deshalb besondere qualifizierte Frauen nachdrücklich auf, sich zu bewerben. Bewerbungen von Menschen mit Schwerbehinderung und ihnen gleichgestellte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt. Sofern Sie möchten, dass Ihre Rechte als schwerbehinderter Mensch oder als einer schwerbehinderten Person gleichgestellter Mensch im Auswahlverfahren berücksichtigt werden, bitten wir Sie, uns dies freiwillig an geeigneter Stelle in Ihrer Bewerbung mitzuteilen (z. B. im Anschreiben oder im Lebenslauf oder an anderer deutlich hervorgehobener Stelle) und einen entsprechenden Nachweis beizufügen (z. B. Kopie des Schwerbehindertenausweises). Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen aller Nationalitäten. Chancengleichheit ist einer unserer zentralen Organisationswerte. Deshalb freuen wir uns über Bewerbungen unabhängig von Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, geschlechtlicher Identität, geschlechtlichem Ausdruck und/oder geschlechtlichem Merkmal, Religion und Weltanschauung, Alter sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität. Wir weisen darauf hin, dass Bewerbungsunterlagen grundsätzlich nicht zurückgesandt werden. Weitere Informationen finden Sie unter: www.tib.eu

items.title: PhD Autonomous & Decentralized Air Traffic Management
items.desc: Functieomschrijving Background Air Traffic Management (ATM) and Communications, Navigation, and Surveillance (CNS) systems form the operational foundation of civil aviation. Current operations depend heavily on centralized ground facilities and satellite services for surveillance and management. This system is vulnerable for a range of disruptions including infrastructure failures, GNSS outages or cyber incidents. These vulnerabilities can degrade or even halt civil aviation. Project ORION (Onboard Resilient Infrastructure-free Operational Network) investigates an alternative ATM/CNS architecture designed to function without reliance on ground- or space-based infrastructure. By utilizing an aeronautical ad-hoc network for communication, relative positioning, and surveillance, ORION aims to enable aircraft to self-organize and maintain safe separation thus ensuring a minimum service level even during (large scale) disruptions. Project Description This PhD project is fundamentally multidisciplinary. As a PhD candidate, you will design, model, and evaluate a decentralized ATM/CNS architecture. The research focuses on determining how core traffic management functions can be sustained through cooperation using an aeronautical network when centralized ground and satellite services are unavailable. In the first phase of the research, you will determine a set of use cases and design the underlying aeronautical ad-hoc networking concept layer to enable direct airborne data exchange, cooperative relative localization, and cooperative surveillance. Next, building on this network layer, you will formulate distributed algorithms for fundamental traffic management functions, including aircraft-as-a-sensor (mesh network), separation assurance, conflict detection and resolution, and traffic sequencing. Finally, to evaluate the operational feasibility of the architecture, you will implement the models within an ATM simulation platform, such as the open-source simulator BlueSky. For this you will extend the platform to include the ad-hoc networking functionality. Using this environment, you will stress-test the system under severe disruption scenarios by comparing the overall performance directly against conventional centralized ATM/CNS operations. This will provide evidence of the performance of the models for the various use-cases. Your profile Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field; Strong analytical and mathematical foundation, with experience in or a keen aptitude for complex systems modelling and distributed systems; Multidisciplinary mindset with the ability to bridge distinct domains: connecting operational ATM concepts with distributed network protocols and algorithm design; Strong background in programming, using Python or other relevant programming languages; Good scientific reporting and communication skills in written and spoken English. What we offer you You will receive a 4-year research contract from NLR and will join the Air Traffic department. In addition, you will be enrolled in the Doctoral Education programme of the Graduate School at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). During this period, you will work closely with NLR colleagues in Amsterdam and with academic supervisors from TU Delft. Your working week will ideally be divided into: 2 days in Amsterdam, 2 days in Delft, and 1 day from home. In Addition, We Offer No fewer than 45 days off (with full-time employment); A fixed end-of-year bonus of 8%; A contribution towards your healthcare costs; Extra paid parental leave; The possibility to work from home where possible. items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology at the University of Oulu (Finland)
items.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are currently looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland. The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) . The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities. The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education. About the job As a doctoral researcher, you will: Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning. Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities . Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers. Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities. Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners. Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results. In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Qualifications To succeed in the position, we expect from you: A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline. A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values. Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research. Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research. Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments. Additional merits considered an advantage Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education . Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers . Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design . Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning . Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments. Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage). What we offer? The support of an experienced and enthusiastic project team of where you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and close-ones in settling into Oulu. We have a HR Excellence in Research -quality label which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, excellent education system, and competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Salary The position is fixed-term for three years as soon as possible or starting from January 2027. The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (maximum of 50% of the job-specific component). Starting gross salary will be approx. 2300-2600 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6months is applied in the position. How to apply? Interested? If yes, please apply by 15.11.2026 (23:59 Finnish local time) through our recruitment system. The application should be written in English and include the following: Cover letter CV following the guidelines of the Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity Certificates/Diplomas Contact information of two persons available for recommendation The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-site or remote interview. All applicants will be notified during the selection process. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, such as people of different ages, genders and lingual, cultural or minority groups. items.title: Doctoral Researcher (Photoacoustic Aerosol and Black Carbon Measurements) / Väitöskirjatutkija (Fotoakustiset aerosoli- ja mustan hiilen mittaukset)
items.desc: Tampere University and Tampere University of Applied Sciences create a unique environment for multidisciplinary, inspirational and high-impact research and education. Our university community has its competitive edges in technology, health and society . www.tuni.fi/en The Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics group, part of the Aerosol Physics Laboratory at Tampere University, is establishing a new research direction in photoacoustic measurement technology within Tampere's strong aerosol research ecosystem. The group brings established expertise in photoacoustic and optical measurements, complemented by the Aerosol Physics Laboratory's long-standing expertise in aerosols and combustion processes. This work builds on monitoring-capable, multi-wavelength photoacoustic instrumentation, including PAAS-4λ, which has been operating at Hyytiälä since 2023. Job Description As a doctoral researcher, you will carry out a focused research project on next-generation photoacoustic methods for aerosol and black-carbon measurements. Your core tasks will be to contribute to the development and construction of a new PAAS instrument version for laboratory testing and characterization, and to develop, test and validate new traceable calibration routines for photoacoustic and optical aerosol measurements. The work combines hands-on instrumentation, laboratory experiments, uncertainty analysis, programming and scientific data analysis. A central motivation is Directive (EU) 2024/2881 on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe, which introduces black-carbon monitoring at urban and rural monitoring supersites. This creates a clear need for accurate, traceable and comparable optical measurements of equivalent black carbon (eBC). As your expertise develops, you will have room to shape your own research questions. Possible directions include analysing existing data from sub-Arctic and Arctic regions, investigating how atmospheric processing changes the optical properties of black carbon, and developing ideas for future measurements. Requirements Applicants must hold an internationally recognized Master's degree in physics, engineering, aerosol or atmospheric science, optics, photonics, environmental science or another relevant field by the starting date. You should be motivated by experimental research, measurement technology and learning across disciplines. The most important qualifications are hands-on experience with scientific instrumentation and strong programming and data-analysis skills in Python, MATLAB or comparable tools. Previous work with black-carbon or photoacoustic instruments is a significant advantage. Experience in aerosol measurements, optics, electronics, data acquisition, calibration or uncertainty analysis is also valuable. Excellent English and constructive teamwork are essential; Finnish is not required. We offer You will receive structured doctoral training and close scientific supervision while developing expertise in experimental aerosol science, optics and advanced measurement technology. You will work closely with the Postdoctoral Researcher recruited alongside this position and with experienced researchers in the group. As your project progresses, you will take increasing responsibility for experiments, analysis, publications and presentations at international conferences. We offer a fixed-term Doctoral Researcher position for three years. The preferred starting date is 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible by mutual agreement. A trial period of six months applies to all our new employees. The salary will be based on both the job requirements and the employee's personal performance in accordance with the Finnish University Salary System. A typical starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is around EUR 3,000 per month. The Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics group has a long record of developing optical instruments for aerosol and cloud research and an extensive network of international collaborators. At Tampere University, this expertise is embedded in the Aerosol Physics Laboratory, adding its strengths in aerosols, combustion processes and measurement technology to a strong interdisciplinary research environment. As a member of staff at Tampere University, you will enjoy a range of competitive benefits, such as occupational health care services, flexible work schedule, versatile research infrastructure, modern teaching facilities and a safe and inviting campus area as well as a personal fund to spend on sports and cultural activities in your free time. Please read more about working at Tampere University and information about Tampere University as an employer. You can also find more information about us and working and living Tampere by watching our video: Tampere Higher Education Community - our academic playground. Finland is among the most stable, free and safe countries in the world, based on prominent ratings by various agencies. Tampere is the largest inland city of Finland, and the city is counted among the major academic hubs in the Nordic countries. Tampere region is the most rapidly growing urban area in Finland and home to a vibrant knowledge-intensive entrepreneurial community. The city is an industrial powerhouse that enjoys a rich cultural scene and a reputation as a centre of Finland’s information society. Tampere is also surrounded by vivid nature with forests and lakes, providing countless opportunities for easy-to-access outdoor adventures and refreshment throughout the year.
